Revealed in Medina.

{1} This is a command from Allah Most High to His believing servants, with what faith requires of them: to fulfil contracts, that is, to complete and perfect them, and not to break or diminish them. This covers the contracts between the servant and his Lord, namely committing to His worship, carrying it out in the most complete manner, and not reducing its rights in any way; the contracts between him and the Messenger, by obeying and following him; the contracts between him and his parents and relatives, by showing them kindness, maintaining ties with them, and not severing them; the contracts between him and his companions, by fulfilling the rights of companionship in wealth and poverty, ease and hardship; and the contracts between him and creation, such as contracts of exchange like sale and lease and the like, and contracts of gratuitous giving like gifts and the like. Moreover, it includes fulfilling the rights of the Muslims which Allah has established among them in His saying: ﴿The believers are but brothers﴾, [by supporting one another] in truth, cooperating in it, being affectionate toward one another among the Muslims, and not cutting one another off. Thus this command encompasses the foundations of the religion and its branches, for all of them fall within the contracts which Allah has commanded to be fulfilled. [From this verse it is deduced that the basic ruling regarding contracts and conditions is permissibility, and that they are concluded by whatever indicates them, whether by speech or action, because of the generality of the verse.]

Then He said, bestowing favour upon His servants: ﴿Lawful for you﴾, that is, for your benefit, out of mercy toward you, ﴿are the beasts of cattle﴾: the camels, cattle, and sheep. Indeed, it may even include the wild ones among them, such as gazelles, wild asses, and similar game. Some of the Companions used this verse as evidence for the permissibility of the fetus that dies in its mother's womb after she is slaughtered. ﴿Except what is recited to you﴾, meaning its prohibition from them, in His saying: ﴿Prohibited to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine ...﴾ to the end of the verse; for these mentioned things, although they are of the beasts of cattle, are prohibited.

Since the permissibility of the beasts of cattle is general in all circumstances and times, He made an exception from it concerning game during the state of ihram, saying: ﴿Not permitting game while you are in ihram﴾, that is: the beasts of cattle are permitted to you in every case, except when you are described as not permitting game while in ihram, that is, as transgressing by killing it while in the state of ihram; for that is not lawful for you if it is game, such as gazelles and the like. Game is the edible wild animal. ﴿Indeed, Allah ordains what He wills﴾, that is, whatever He wills, He decrees with a ruling that accords with His wisdom, just as He commanded you to fulfil contracts, for the attainment of your interests and the averting of harms from you; and He made lawful for you the beasts of cattle out of mercy toward you, and prohibited for you what is excluded from them among those with particular conditions, such as carrion and the like, as protection and honour for you, and the game of ihram out of reverence and magnification of the state of ihram.

{2} The Exalted says: "O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allah" — that is, His sacred prohibitions, which He has commanded you to honour and not to commit. The prohibition covers both the prohibition of doing them and the prohibition of believing them to be permissible. It therefore includes the prohibition of committing what is ugly and of believing it to be lawful, and it includes the prohibitions of the state of ihram (iḥrām, the sacred state of pilgrimage) and the prohibitions of the Sacred Precinct (al-ḥaram, the sanctuary around Makkah). Also included is what He specified in His words: "nor the sacred month" — that is, do not violate it by fighting in it or by any other kind of wrongdoing. As Allah the Exalted says: "Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the register of Allah from the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them, four are sacred. That is the correct religion, so do not wrong yourselves therein."

Most of the scholars hold that fighting in the sacred months has been abrogated (mansūkh, abrogated) by the words of Allah the Exalted: "And when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them," and by other general texts which command fighting the disbelievers without restriction and threaten those who hold back from fighting them without restriction. They also cite the fact that the Prophet (ﷺ) fought the people of al-Ṭāʾif in Dhū al-Qaʿdah, which is one of the sacred months.

Others said: the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months is not abrogated, because of this verse and other texts that specifically prohibit it. They interpreted the unrestricted texts that relate to this in light of these, and said: "The unrestricted is interpreted in light of the restricted." Some of them made a distinction, saying: it is not permissible to begin fighting in the sacred months, but continuing it and completing it is permissible if it began outside them. They applied the Prophet's (ﷺ) fighting against the people of al-Ṭāʾif to this, because the start of their fighting was at Ḥunayn in Shawwāl.

All of this concerns fighting that is not intended for defence. As for defensive fighting, if the disbelievers initiate fighting against the Muslims, then it is permissible for the Muslims to fight in defence of themselves in the sacred month and otherwise, by the consensus of the scholars.

His words: "nor the offering, nor the garlands" — that is, do not violate the offering that is brought to the House of Allah for ḥajj or ʿumrah or other purposes, of camels or other animals. Do not prevent it from reaching its place of sacrifice, do not seize it by theft or otherwise, do not neglect it or burden it beyond its capacity out of fear that it will perish before reaching its place; rather, honour it and honour those who bring it. "Nor the garlands": this is a particular kind of offering, namely the offering to which garlands or straps are braided and placed around its neck, to display the rites of Allah, to encourage people to follow, to teach them the Sunnah, and so that it is recognised as an offering and thus respected. For this reason, garlanding the offering is among the recommended Sunnahs and rites.

"Nor those coming to the Sacred House" — that is, those intending it. "Seeking bounty from their Lord and His pleasure" — that is, whoever intends this Sacred House, whether his intention is Allah's bounty through trade and lawful gains, or his intention is Allah's pleasure through his ḥajj and ʿumrah, circumambulation of it, prayer and other kinds of worship: do not approach him with harm, nor humiliate him; rather, honour him and honour those who come to visit the House of your Lord. Included in this command is the command to secure the roads leading to the House of Allah, and to make those who intend it feel safe and at ease, unafraid for their lives or anything less than that, and unafraid for their property from unjust taxes, plunder and the like.

This noble verse is specified by the words of the Exalted: "O you who have believed, the polytheists are only impure, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Ḥarām after this, their year." So the polytheist is not permitted to enter the Sacred Precinct. The specification in this verse of the prohibition against interfering with one who intends the House seeking Allah's bounty or His pleasure indicates that whoever intends it in order to commit sin therein, the complete respect for the Sacred Precinct requires that he be prevented from corrupting the House of Allah in this condition, as Allah the Exalted says: "And whoever intends therein deviation by wrongdoing, We will make him taste a painful punishment."

When He forbade them from hunting in the state of ihram, He said: "And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt." That is, when you have exited the state of ihram of ḥajj and ʿumrah [and left the Sacred Precinct], hunting becomes permissible for you and that prohibition is removed. A command after a prohibition returns things to what they were before.

"Nor let the hatred of a people—that they obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām—lead you to transgress." That is: let not the hatred, enmity and aggression of a people towards you, in that they prevented you from the Masjid, drive you to transgress against them in seeking to satisfy yourselves through them. The servant must adhere to the command of Allah and follow the path of justice, even if he is wronged, harmed or transgressed against. It is not lawful for him to lie to one who lied to him, or to betray one who betrayed him.

"And cooperate in righteousness and piety" — that is, let some of you help one another in righteousness. Righteousness (al-birr) is a comprehensive term for everything Allah loves and is pleased with, of outward and inward deeds, of the rights of Allah and the rights of the children of Adam. Piety (al-taqwā) in this context is a comprehensive term for abandoning everything that Allah and His Messenger dislike, of outward and inward deeds, and every quality of goodness that is commanded to be done, or quality of evil that is commanded to be abandoned. The servant is commanded to perform these himself and to help his fellow believing brothers to perform them by every word that encourages them and enlivens them towards them, and by every such action.

"And do not cooperate in sin and transgression" — sin (al-ithm) is daring to commit acts of disobedience for which the doer incurs sin and blame; transgression (al-ʿudwān) is overstepping against people in their lives, property and honour. Every sin and every wrong, the servant must restrain himself from it, and then help others to abandon it.

"And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in punishment" — upon whoever disobeys Him and dares to violate His prohibitions. So beware of the prohibitions, lest His punishment, both in this world and in the Hereafter, befall you.

{3} This is what Allah has made known to us in His words: {except what is recited to you}. Know that Allah, blessed and exalted, prohibits nothing except to safeguard His servants and protect them from the harm present in what is forbidden. He may make this clear to His servants or He may not. He informed us that He has forbidden {carrion} (al-maytah), and by carrion is meant that whose life has departed without a lawful slaughter (dhakah shar'iyyah). It is forbidden because of its harm, which is the congestion of blood within its body and its flesh, which harms the one who eats it. Often it dies from an illness that causes its destruction, and so it harms the one who eats it. Excepted from this are the carrion of locusts and fish, for these are lawful. {And blood}, that is, poured-forth blood, as it is restricted in the other verse. {And the flesh of swine}: this includes all its parts. Allah specified it among the other filthy things, and among the predators, because a group of the People of the Book, the Christians, claim that Allah has made it lawful for them. So do not be deceived by them; rather, it is forbidden as one of the filthy things. {And that which has been dedicated to other than Allah}, that is, over which the name of other than Allah [exalted be He] has been invoked, such as idols, saints, stars, and other created beings. Just as the mention of Allah's name makes the slaughtered animal good, the mention of the name of another over it gives it a spiritual impurity, because it is shirk with Allah, exalted be He. {And the strangled animal}, that is, one that dies by being strangled with a hand, a rope, or by putting its head into something narrow so that it cannot get it out and dies. {And the beaten animal}, that is, one that dies from being struck with a stick, a stone, a piece of wood, or having something fall upon it, intentionally or unintentionally. {And the fallen animal}, that is, one that falls from a height, such as a mountain, a wall, a roof, or the like, and dies from that. {And the gored animal}, which is one that is gored by another and dies. {And that which a predator has eaten}: from a wolf, a lion, a tiger, or from birds that prey upon game; for if it dies because a predator has eaten from it, it is not lawful. His words {except what you have slaughtered} refer to these cases: the strangled, the beaten, the fallen, the gored, and the one partly eaten by a predator, if it is slaughtered while life remains in it stably, so that the slaughter is effective. For this reason the jurists said: if a predator or something else has split open its entrails or cut its throat, then the existence of its life is like its non-existence, since slaughter gives no benefit in that case. Some of them required only the existence of life; so if one slaughters it while life is in it, it is lawful, even if its entrails have been split open, and this is the apparent meaning of the noble verse. {And that you seek decision through the arrows}: that is, the forbidding of seeking the decision of the arrows. The meaning of seeking decision (istiqsam) is seeking what is apportioned to you and decreed for you through them. They were three arrow-shafts used in the pre-Islamic period: one had written on it "do," another "do not," and the third was blank with nothing written on it. When one of them intended a journey, a marriage, or the like, he shuffled these arrows, which were equal in size, and then drew out one of them. If the one marked "do" came out, he proceeded with his affair; if the one marked "do not" came out, he refrained and did not proceed with his matter; and if the blank one came out, he repeated the drawing until one of the two arrows came out, and acted accordingly. Allah forbade them this practice, in this form and what resembles it, and in its place gave them istikharah (seeking the good from their Lord) in all their affairs. {That is grave disobedience}: the reference is to all the prohibitions mentioned above, which Allah forbade to safeguard His servants, and that they are {fisq}, that is, departure from His obedience into the obedience of Satan.

Then He bestowed favor upon His servants by His words: {Today those who disbelieve have despaired of your religion, so do not fear them but fear Me. Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and approved for you Islam as a religion. But whoever is compelled by hunger, not inclined toward sin, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.}

The day referred to is the Day of Arafat, when Allah perfected their religion, granted victory to His servant and messenger, and utterly humiliated the people of polytheism, after they had been eager to turn the believers away from their religion and had hoped to do so. When they saw the might, triumph, and dominance of Islam, they despaired completely of the believers returning to their religion, and they came to fear and dread them. For this reason, in that year in which the Prophet (ﷺ) performed the Farewell Pilgrimage, in the tenth year (AH), no polytheist performed the pilgrimage and no one circumambulated the House naked. Therefore He said: {So do not fear them but fear Me}, that is, do not fear the polytheists; fear Allah, who gave you victory over them, humiliated them, and turned their plots back upon their own necks. {Today I have perfected for you your religion}: by the completion of victory and the perfection of the laws, both outward and inward, in their fundamentals and their branches.

For this reason the Book and the Sunnah are entirely sufficient in the rulings of the religion, its fundamentals and its branches. Every pretentious person who claims that people must, in knowing their beliefs and rulings, rely on sciences other than the knowledge of the Book and the Sunnah, such as speculative theology (ilm al-kalam) and the like, is ignorant and mistaken in his claim. He has asserted that the religion is not complete except by what he has said and called to, and this is among the greatest injustices and ignorance regarding Allah and His Messenger. {And I have completed My favor upon you}: both outward and inward. {And I have approved for you Islam as a religion}: that is, I have chosen and selected it for you as a religion, just as I have approved you for it. So stand by it in gratitude to your Lord, and praise the One who has blessed you with the best, most noble, and most complete of religions. {Whoever is compelled}: that is, one whom necessity has driven to eat something of the prohibited things mentioned earlier in His words: {Prohibited to you are carrion}. {By hunger}: that is, by famine. {Not inclined toward sin}: that is, not deviating toward wrongdoing, by not eating until compelled, and not exceeding in eating beyond what suffices. {Indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful}: in that He permitted him to eat in this state, and showed mercy to him by what sustains his body, without any deficiency reaching his religion.

{4} Almighty God says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): {They ask you what has been made lawful for them}: of foods. {Say: What is good (al-tayyibat) has been made lawful for you}: and it is everything that has benefit or pleasure without harm to the body or the mind. Included in this are all grains and fruits found in towns and in the deserts, and included are all the animals of the sea and all the land animals, except what the Lawgiver has excluded, such as predatory beasts and the noxious (al-khaba'ith) among them. For this reason the verse indicates, by implication, the prohibition of the noxious, as stated explicitly in His words: {And he makes lawful for them the good things and forbids for them the noxious things} (7:157). {And what you have taught of the hunting animals (al-jawarih)}; that is: and there has been made lawful for you what you have taught of the hunting animals ... to the end of the verse.

This verse indicates several matters:

First: God's kindness to His servants and His mercy toward them, in that He has widened for them the paths of what is lawful, and permitted them what hunting animals catch which they have not slaughtered. By "al-jawarih" (hunting animals) is meant dogs, cheetahs, falcons and the like, which catch with their fangs or their talons.

Second: It is required that they be trained (mu'allamah) in a manner that is recognized as training by custom: that it runs when released, returns when called, and when it holds the prey it does not eat. For this reason He says: {Teach them of what God has taught you, so eat of what they hold for you} (5:4); that is, what they hold back from the game for your sake. And what the hunting animal eats from it is not lawful, for one does not know that it held it for its owner, and perhaps it held it for itself.

Third: The requirement that the dog or bird or the like wound the prey. This is based on His words {of the hunting animals}, together with what preceded regarding the prohibition of the strangled animal (al-munkhaniqah). So if the dog or other animal strangles it, or kills it by its weight, it is not permitted. This is based on the view that the hunting animals are those that wound the prey with their fangs or talons. The well-known view, however, is that "al-jawarih" means "al-kawasib," that is, those that obtain the prey and attain it; thus there is no indication in the verse on this view. And God knows best.

Fourth: The permissibility of keeping a hunting dog, as related in the authentic hadith, even though keeping a dog is prohibited, because permitting its hunting and training entails permitting its keeping.

Fifth: The purity of what the mouth of the dog touches of the game, because God permitted it and did not mention washing for it, which indicates its purity.

Sixth: In it is the excellence of knowledge, and that the hunting animal that has been trained through knowledge is permitted to hunt, while the untrained is not permitted to hunt.

Seventh: That occupying oneself with training a dog, a bird or the like is not blameworthy and is not of the frivolous or vain, but is rather a purposeful matter, since it is a means to the lawfulness of its game and benefiting from it.

Eighth: In it is an argument for one who permits the sale of a hunting dog; he said: because it may not be obtained except by that.

Ninth: In it is the requirement of mentioning God's name upon releasing the hunting animal, and that if one deliberately does not mention God's name, what the hunting animal kills is not permitted.

Tenth: That it is permissible to eat what the hunting animal catches, whether or not the animal killed it, and that if its owner reaches it while it still has stable life in it, it is not permitted except by slaughtering it.

Then He urged them to be mindful of Him and warned against the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection, and that this matter has drawn near and approached, so He said: {And fear God; indeed God is swift in reckoning}.

{5} The Exalted repeated the permissibility of good things to show favor (imtinan), and as a call to the servants to thank Him and to remember Him often; for He permitted them what their need calls for and what benefit they gain from the good things. {And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you} — that is: the slaughtered animals of the Jews and Christians are lawful for you, O company of Muslims, but not the slaughtered animals of the rest of the disbelievers, for their slaughter is not lawful for the Muslims. This is because the People of the Book trace their lineage to the prophets and the scriptures, and all the messengers agreed on the prohibition of slaughtering for other than God, since that is shirk; so the Jews and Christians hold as part of their religion the prohibition of slaughtering for other than God, and therefore their slaughtered animals were made lawful, to the exclusion of others. The evidence that by "their food" is meant their slaughtered animals is that food which is not slaughtered, such as grains and fruits, has no special status for the People of the Book in this respect; rather such food is permitted even if it comes from others. Also, He attributed the food to them, which indicates that it was food by virtue of their slaughter. It cannot be said that this is for ownership, and that what is meant is food that they own, because that is not permitted when taken by usurpation, nor from the Muslims. {And your food} — O Muslims — {is lawful for them}; that is, it is lawful for you to feed them with it. {And} there were made lawful for you {the chaste women} — that is, the free, virtuous women — {from among the believing women}; and the free, virtuous women {from among those who were given the Scripture before you} — that is, from among the Jews and Christians. This specifies His statement: {And do not marry the polytheistic women until they believe}. The implication of the verse is that the female slaves among the believing women are not permitted for free men to marry, and that is so. As for the People of the Book women, in every case they are not permitted, and their marriage is not lawful for free men absolutely, because of His statement: {from your believing young women}. As for Muslim women when they are slaves, it is not lawful for free men to marry them except under two conditions: lack of ability to afford a free woman's marriage (ṭawl), and fear of falling into sin (ʿanat). As for the immoral women who are not chaste from fornication, their marriage is not permitted, whether they are Muslims or People of the Book, until they repent; because of His statement: {The fornicating man does not marry except a fornicating woman or a polytheist...} — the verse. And His statement: {when you have given them their wages} — that is, We have permitted you to marry them when you give them their dowries; so whoever resolves not to give her her dowry, she is not lawful for him. He commanded giving it to them if she is mature and fit to receive it; otherwise the husband gives it to her guardian. The attribution of the wages to them is evidence that the woman owns her entire dowry, and no one has any share of it except what she permits to her husband, her guardian, or others. {Chaste, not fornicating} — that is, while you, the husbands, are chaste toward your wives through guarding your private parts from others, {not fornicating} — that is, not committing fornication with anyone, {nor taking secret lovers} — this is fornication with paramours; for among the fornicators in the Jahiliyyah, some would fornicate with whoever came along, and this is the fornicator (musafih), and some would fornicate with their intimate friend and beloved; so God the Exalted informed that all of this contradicts chastity, and that the condition of marriage is that the man be chaste from fornication.

And His statement, the Exalted: {And whoever disbelieves in faith, his deed has become worthless} — that is: whoever disbelieves in God the Exalted, or in what it is obligatory to believe in of His books and messengers, or in any part of the legal rulings, his deed has become worthless; on condition that he dies upon his disbelief, as He said: {And whoever of you reverts from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever — those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter}. {And he, in the Hereafter, is among the losers} — that is, those who lost themselves, their wealth, and their families on the Day of Resurrection, and attained everlasting wretchedness.

This is a great verse, containing many rulings. We will mention those that God has made easy and accessible:

First: Carrying out these commands and acting upon them is a requirement of faith, which is not complete without it. This is because He introduced them with His words, ﴿O you who have believed﴾, through to the end of the verse. That is, "O you who have believed, act in accordance with the demands of your faith in what We have legislated for you."

Second: The command to stand up for prayer (salah), based on His words, ﴿when you rise to prayer﴾.

Third: The command to have intention (niyyah) for prayer, based on His words, ﴿when you rise to prayer﴾, that is, with the intention and purpose of performing it.

Fourth: Purity (taharah) is a condition for the validity of prayer, because God commanded purification when rising to pray, and the default in a command is obligation.

Fifth: Purification is not obligatory upon the entry of the prayer time, but becomes obligatory when one intends to pray.

Sixth: Every act that is called "prayer", whether obligatory, voluntary, a communal obligation (fard al-kifayah), or the funeral prayer (salat al-janazah), requires purity. According to many scholars, this even applies to prostration on its own, such as the prostration of recitation (sujud al-tilawah) and the prostration of gratitude (sujud al-shukr).

Seventh: The command to wash the face, which is the area encompassed by facing, from the normal hairline to what descends below the jaw-bones and the chin in length, and from ear to ear in width. It includes rinsing the mouth and the nose (madmadah and istinshaq) according to the Sunnah. It also includes the hair on it: if the hair is sparse, water must reach the skin; if it is thick, its outer layer suffices.

Eighth: The command to wash the hands, and that their limit is the elbows. As most exegetes said, ﴿to﴾ here means "with," as in His words, ﴿and do not consume their wealth with your wealth﴾. Also, the obligation cannot be fulfilled without washing the entire elbow.

Ninth: The command to wipe the head.

Tenth: It is obligatory to wipe all of it, because the particle "bi" (in the verse) does not denote partiality, but rather adjacency, and the wiping must cover the entire head.

Eleventh: Wiping is sufficient in any manner, whether with both hands, one hand, a cloth, a stick, or similar, because God stated wiping without restricting it to a specific manner, which indicates its generality.

Twelfth: The obligation is wiping. So if one washes the head without passing the hand over it, it is not sufficient, because he has not done what God commanded.

Thirteenth: The command to wash the feet up to the ankles, and what is said about them is the same as what is said about the hands.

Fourteenth: In it is a refutation of the al-Rafidah (a Shi'i sect) according to the recitation of the majority, which reads the word in the accusative case, and that it is impermissible to wipe them while they are uncovered.

Fifteenth: In it is an indication of wiping over leather socks (khuffayn), according to the reading in the genitive case of ﴿and your feet﴾. Each of the two readings is understood in terms of a meaning: according to the accusative reading, the feet must be washed if they are uncovered; according to the genitive reading, they are wiped if they are covered by socks.

Sixteenth: The command to follow the order in wudu', because God mentioned the body parts in sequence, and because He placed a part to be wiped (the head) between two parts to be washed, and no benefit for this is known other than the sequence.

Seventeenth: The sequence is specific to the four body parts mentioned in this verse. As for the sequence between rinsing the mouth and nose and the face, or between the right and left hands and feet, this is not obligatory. Rather, it is recommended to precede rinsing the mouth and nose before washing the face, to start with the right before the left hand and foot, and to precede wiping the head before wiping the ears.

Eighteenth: The command to renew wudu' for each prayer, so that the form of what was commanded exists.

Nineteenth: The command to perform ghusl (full bathing) from janabah (major ritual impurity).

Twentieth: It is obligatory to generalize the washing to the entire body, because God attributed purification to the body and did not restrict it to any particular part.

Twenty-first: The command to wash the outer and inner parts of the hair in janabah.

Twenty-second: The minor impurity (hadath asghar) is subsumed under the major impurity (hadath akbar), and it is sufficient for one who is in both states to intend and then generalize the washing of the body. This is because God mentioned only purification and did not mention repeating wudu'.

Twenty-third: The term janub (one in janabah) applies to one who has ejaculated (mani) while awake or asleep, or who has had intercourse even without ejaculation.

Twenty-fourth: One who mentions that he had a wet dream but found no wetness is not required to perform ghusl, because janabah has not been confirmed in his case.

Twenty-fifth: Mention of God's favor upon His servants by legislating tayammum (dry ablution).

Twenty-sixth: One of the reasons that permits tayammum is the presence of an illness that would be harmed by washing with water, so tayammum is permissible for him.

Twenty-seventh: Among the reasons permitting it are travel, and coming from urination or defecation when water is unavailable. Illness permits tayammum even when water is present, due to the harm it would cause. The rest of the reasons permit it only when water is absent, even if one is at home.

Twenty-eighth: What exits from the two passages (urine and feces) invalidates wudu'.

Twenty-ninth: Those who said that only these two matters invalidate wudu' used this verse as evidence. Therefore, it is not invalidated by touching the private parts nor by anything else.

Thirtieth: The recommendation to use euphemism for what is repulsive to pronounce, based on His words, ﴿or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself﴾.

Thirty-first: Touching a woman with desire and lust invalidates wudu'.

Thirty-second: The condition that water be absent for the validity of tayammum.

Thirty-third: If water is present, even during prayer, tayammum is nullified, because God only permitted it when water is absent.

Thirty-fourth: If the prayer time enters and one has no water, he is obligated to search for it in his baggage and in what is nearby, because it is not said that one "did not find" water to someone who did not search.

Thirty-fifth: If one finds water that is insufficient for all of his purification, he is obligated to use it, and then perform tayammum afterward.

Thirty-sixth: Water that has changed in color or smell by pure substances takes precedence over tayammum; that is, it remains purifying. This is because water that has changed is still water, and so it falls under His words, ﴿and you find no water﴾.

Thirty-seventh: The intention for tayammum is necessary, based on His words, ﴿then perform tayammum﴾, that is, intend.

Thirty-eighth: It is sufficient to perform tayammum with anything that rises from the surface of the earth, such as dust or other things. According to this, His words, ﴿then wipe your faces and hands with it﴾, are either a matter of generalizing the usual case, since dust commonly has fine particles that cling to the face and hands when wiped, or are a guide to what is better, meaning that if dust with fine particles is available, it is preferable.

Thirty-ninth: Tayammum with impure dust is not valid, because it is not pure but impure.

Fortieth: In tayammum, only the face and the two hands are wiped, not the remaining body parts.

Forty-first: His words, ﴿your faces﴾, cover the entire face, and it must all be wiped. However, it is excused if dust enters the mouth and nose, or what lies beneath the hair, even if the hair is sparse.

Forty-second: The hands are wiped only up to the wrists, because "hands" when stated without qualification means that. If it were required to wipe up to the forearms, God would have restricted it with that, as He did in wudu'.

Forty-third: The verse is general regarding the permissibility of tayammum for all states of impurity, both major and minor, and even the impurity of the body, because God made it a substitute for purification with water and stated it without restriction. However, it may be said that impurity of the body does not fall under the ruling of tayammum, because the context concerns the states of ritual impurity (ahdath), and this is the view of the majority of scholars.

Forty-fourth: The place of tayammum is the same for both minor and major impurity, namely the face and the two hands.

Forty-fifth: If one who is in two states of impurity intends tayammum for both, it suffices, based on the generality and unrestricted wording of the verse.

Forty-sixth: Wiping is sufficient with whatever is in one's hand or otherwise, because God said, ﴿then wipe﴾, and did not mention what is used for wiping, which indicates that it is permissible with anything.

Forty-seventh: The sequence is a condition in the purification of tayammum, just as it is a condition in wudu', and because God began with wiping the face before wiping the hands.

Forty-eighth: In what He has legislated for us, God has not placed upon us any hardship, difficulty, or strain. Rather, it is a mercy from Him toward His servants, to purify them and to complete His favor upon them, and this is it.

Forty-ninth: Purification of the outward by water and dust completes the purification of the inward by monotheism (tawhid) and sincere repentance (tawbah nasuh).

Fiftieth: Although tayammum does not have the cleanliness and purity perceived by the senses and observation, it contains a spiritual purity arising from obedience to God's command.

Fifty-first: A servant should reflect upon the wisdom and secrets in God's legislation concerning purification and other matters, so that he increases in knowledge and understanding, and increases in gratitude to God and love for Him for the rulings He has legislated, which lead the servant to lofty and elevated stations.

{7} God commands His servants to remember His blessings, both religious and worldly, with their hearts and tongues. For continually remembering them calls one to thank God, to love Him, and to fill the heart with His kindness. It also removes self-admiration (ʻujb) at one's religious blessings and increases one's share of God's grace and kindness. {And His covenant} — that is, remember His covenant {which He made with you}, namely the pledge He took from you. This does not mean that they uttered or spoke the covenant and pledge aloud; rather, it means that by their faith in God and His Messenger they have committed themselves to obeying them both. Hence He said: {when you said, "We hear and we obey."} That is, we hear what You have called us to of Your verses, both the Qur'anic and the cosmic, with understanding, submission and compliance; and we obey by carrying out what You have commanded us and by avoiding what You have forbidden us. This covers all the laws of religion, both outward and inward. The believers remember in this the covenant of God and His pledge upon them, keep it in mind, and strive to fulfil what they were commanded completely and without deficiency. {And fear God}: in all your circumstances. {Indeed, God is Knowing of what is in the breasts} — that is, of what they harbour of thoughts, secrets and inner impulses. So beware lest He perceive in your hearts a matter that He does not approve, or that you do something He dislikes. Fill your hearts with knowledge of Him, love for Him, and sincere goodwill toward His servants; for if you are like this, He will forgive your misdeeds and multiply your good deeds, knowing the soundness of your hearts.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 5, verse 8:

{8} Meaning: {O you who have believed}: by what they were commanded to believe in, uphold the necessary requirements of your faith, by being {qawwamina lillah shuhada'a bil-qist} (steadfast in upholding justice for Allah, witnesses in justice). Let your outward and inward movements be energised to uphold justice, and let that upholding be for Allah alone and not for any worldly purpose, and be intent upon justice, which is equity, neither excessive nor deficient in your words or your actions. Uphold this towards the near and the distant, the friend and the enemy. {And let not the hatred of a people prompt you}; i.e., let not the hatred of a people move you {to not act justly}, as one does who has no justice or equity, but rather, as you bear witness for your ally, bear witness against him, and as you bear witness against your enemy, bear witness for him, even if he is a disbeliever or an innovator. For justice towards him is obligatory, and accepting the truth he brings is obligatory, [because it is true], not because he said it, and the truth is not to be rejected on account of his saying it, for that is an injustice to the truth. {Be just; that is nearer to piety}; i.e., whenever you are keen upon justice and strive in acting by it, that is nearer to the piety of your hearts; and when justice is complete, piety is complete. {Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do}; so He will recompense you for your deeds, good and bad, small and great, with a reward both prompt and deferred.

{9} That is: {Allah has promised} — He who never breaks His promise, and He is the most truthful of speakers — {those who believe in Him, His books, His messengers and the Last Day, and do righteous deeds}: obligatory and recommended ones. {For them is forgiveness} — by pardoning their sins and their consequences — {and a great reward} whose greatness none knows except Allah, the Exalted. {No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do.}

{10} {And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs}: which indicate the clear truth, so they denied them after the realities had been made manifest. {Those are the companions of the Blazing Fire}: those who abide in it constantly, as a companion abides with his companion.

{9} That is: {Allah has promised} — He who never breaks His promise, and He is the most truthful of speakers — {those who believe in Him, His books, His messengers and the Last Day, and do righteous deeds}: obligatory and recommended ones. {For them is forgiveness} — by pardoning their sins and their consequences — {and a great reward} whose greatness none knows except Allah, the Exalted. {No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do.}

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 5, verse 11:

{11} He (Exalted is He) reminds His believing servants of His great blessings, and urges them to remember them with the heart and the tongue. And just as they count their killing of their enemies, their seizing of their wealth, their lands, and their captives as a blessing, so too let them count His favour upon them in restraining their enemies' hands from them and turning their plot back upon their own necks as a blessing. For the enemies had resolved upon a matter and thought they were capable of it; so when they do not achieve their aim against the believers, that is a victory from Allah for His believing servants. They should thank Allah for this, worship Him, and remember Him. This includes everyone who intended harm against the believers, whether an unbeliever, a hypocrite, or a transgressor, whose evil Allah restrained from the Muslims, for he is included in this verse. Then He commanded them with that by which they may seek help in gaining victory over their enemy and in all their affairs, saying: {And upon Allah let the believers rely}; that is, they should depend upon Him in bringing about their religious and worldly benefits, disown their own might and power, and trust in Allah Most High for the attainment of what they love. The measure of a servant's reliance (tawakkul) is according to the measure of his faith, and it is among the obligations of the heart agreed upon.

{12} He, exalted is He, informs that He took from the Children of Israel a heavy, emphatic covenant. He mentions the nature of the covenant, their reward if they fulfil it, and their sin if they do not fulfil it. Then He mentions that they did not fulfil it, and mentions the punishment with which He afflicted them. So He says: ﴿And Allah had certainly taken the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾; that is, their firm and binding pledge. ﴿And We appointed from among them twelve leaders﴾; that is, a chief and overseer over those beneath them, to watch over them, urging them to carry out what they were commanded, calling them to it with insistence. ﴿And Allah said﴾ to the leaders who bore the burdens they bore: ﴿Indeed, I am with you﴾; that is, with help and support, for aid is in proportion to the burden. Then He mentions what He pledged to them, saying: ﴿If you establish prayer﴾ outwardly and inwardly, by performing what is required and proper in it and being constant in that; ﴿and give zakah﴾ to its rightful recipients; ﴿and believe in My messengers﴾, all of them, the best and most complete of whom is Muhammad (ﷺ); ﴿and support them﴾; that is, honour them, and render what is due to them of respect and obedience; ﴿and loan Allah a goodly loan﴾, which is charity and kindness issuing from sincerity, sincere intention and good earnings. So if you do that, ﴿I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. Thus He combined for them the attainment of what is loved, namely Paradise and its bliss, with the removal of what is disliked, namely the expiation of sins and the averting of the punishments that follow from them. ﴿And whoever disbelieves after that﴾, after this covenant and firm pledge confirmed by oaths and obligations, accompanied by encouragement through mention of its reward, ﴿has certainly strayed from the sound way﴾; that is, deliberately and knowingly, so he deserves what the astray deserve of deprivation of reward and incurring of punishment.

{13} It is as if it were said: I wonder, what did they do? Did they fulfil what they covenanted with Allah, or did they break it? So He made clear that they broke it, saying: ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant﴾; that is, because of it We punished them with several punishments:
First: We ﴿cursed them﴾; that is, We drove them away and removed them from Our mercy, since they closed off for themselves the doors of mercy and did not fulfil the covenant that was taken from them, which is its greatest cause.
Second: His saying: ﴿And We made their hearts hard﴾; that is, rigid, such that admonitions do not benefit them and warnings and signs do not profit them; so no enticement moves them to desire and no intimidation stirs them. This is among the greatest punishments upon a servant: that his heart should be of this description, in which guidance and goodness yield nothing but evil.
Third: They distort words from their places; that is, they were afflicted with alteration and substitution, giving the words that Allah intended a meaning other than what Allah and His Messenger intended.
Fourth: They ﴿forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of﴾; for they were reminded of the Torah and what Allah revealed to Moses, and they forgot a portion of it. This includes forgetting its knowledge, so it was lost to them and much of it was not found, as a punishment from Him, and it includes forgetting the action, which is abandonment, so they were not granted success in carrying out what they were commanded. From this is derived a proof against the People of the Book regarding their denial of some of what is mentioned in their Book, or what occurred in their time, which they claim they have forgotten.
Fifth: Continuous treachery, such that ﴿you will not cease to discover treachery from them﴾; that is, treachery against Allah and against His believing servants. Among the greatest of their treacheries is their concealment from those who advise them and think well of them in the right way, and their persistence in their disbelief; this is a great treachery.
These blameworthy traits are present in everyone who possesses their characteristics: whoever does not carry out what Allah commanded and what was taken from him as a binding obligation has a share of the curse, hardness of heart, affliction with the distortion of words, failure to be granted what is right, forgetting a portion of what he was reminded of, and inevitably being afflicted with treachery. We ask Allah for well-being.
Allah called what they were reminded of a "portion" (ḥaẓẓ) because it is the greatest of portions, and all else is merely worldly portions, as He said: ﴿So he went out to his people in his adornment. Those who desired the life of this world said, "Oh, would that we had like what Qarun was given. Indeed, he is one of great fortune."﴾ And He said regarding the beneficial portion: ﴿And none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune.﴾
As for His saying: ﴿except for a few of them﴾; that is, they fulfilled what they covenanted with Allah, so He granted them success and guided them to the straight path. ﴿So pardon them and overlook﴾; that is, do not hold them accountable for the harm that comes from them which would call for their being pardoned; pardon and overlook, for that is kindness. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.﴾ Ihsan (excellence) is that you worship Allah as though you see Him; and if you do not see Him, then He sees you. Regarding the rights of created beings, it is giving them benefit, both religious and worldly.

{14} That is: Just as We took a covenant and pledge from the Jews, so too did We take one from those who said, "We are Christians," [the followers] of Jesus son of Mary. They credited themselves with faith in Allah and His messengers and in what they brought, yet they broke the covenant and forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of, both through knowledge-forgetting and through practice-forgetting. ﴿So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection.﴾ That is: We empowered some of them over others, and among them arose such evils and grudges as necessitate hatred and enmity of some toward others until the Day of Resurrection. This is an observed reality, for the Christians have never ceased, and still do not cease, to be in hatred, enmity, and discord. ﴿And Allah will inform them of what they used to do﴾: and He will punish them for it.

{15} When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned what He had taken as a covenant from the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, and that they broke it, except for a few of them, He commanded them all to believe in Muhammad (ﷺ), and He argued against them with a decisive sign proving the truth of his prophethood. That sign is that he makes clear to them much of what they conceal from the people, even from the common folk of their own religious community. If they are the ones referred to as the people of knowledge, and no one at that time has knowledge of this except what they possess, then the one eager for knowledge has no way to attain it except from them. So the coming of the Messenger (ﷺ) with this magnificent Qur'an, through which he made clear what they were concealing among themselves, while he was unlettered, neither reading nor writing, is among the strongest proofs for the certainty of his messengership. Such is the description of Muhammad in their books, the presence of glad tidings about him in their books, the clarification of the verse of stoning (al-rajm) ... and similar matters. {And He pardons much} means: He leaves aside the explanation of what wisdom does not require. {There has come to you from Allah a light} means: this is the Qur'an, by which one is guided in the darkness of ignorance and the blindness of error. {And a clear Book} means: it clarifies everything that creation needs of the affairs of their religion and their worldly life, from the knowledge of Allah, His names, attributes and acts, and from the knowledge of His legislative rulings and His rulings concerning recompense.

{16} Then He mentioned who it is that is guided by this Qur'an, and what is the means on the servant's part for attaining that, saying: {By it Allah guides whoever follows His pleasure to the ways of peace}. That is: He guides whoever strives and endeavors to attain the pleasure of Allah and whose intention becomes good, to the paths of peace (subul al-salam), by which its follower is saved from punishment and which lead him to the Abode of Peace (dar al-salam). This is knowledge of the truth and acting upon it, in summary and in detail. And He brings them out of the darkness of disbelief, innovation, disobedience, ignorance and heedlessness, into the light of faith, the Sunnah, obedience, knowledge and remembrance. All of these are part of guidance by the permission of Allah, who wills what He wills and what He does not will does not come to be. {And He guides them to a straight path}.

{17} When He, exalted is He, mentioned the taking of the covenant from the People of the Two Scriptures, and that they did not uphold it but broke it, He mentioned their monstrous statements. He mentioned the saying of the Christians, a saying that no one else has said: that God is the Messiah, son of Mary. The basis of their confusion is that he was born without a father. So they held this false belief about him, even though Eve is his counterpart, created without a mother, and Adam is more deserving than him, created without a father or a mother. Why then did they not claim divinity for both of them, as they claimed it for the Messiah? This shows that their saying is following desire without proof or doubt. So God refuted them with clear rational proofs, saying: ﴿Say: Who then has any power against God, if He wished to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother, and everyone on earth altogether?﴾ If those mentioned have no protection that would prevent them, were God to wish to destroy them, and no power to resist that, this shows the invalidity of the divinity of one who cannot prevent destruction and has no power over escape. Among the proofs: ﴿to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ alone, He disposes over them by His cosmic, legislative and retributive decree, while they are owned and managed. Is it fitting that the owned, poor servant be a worshipped god, wholly self-sufficient? This is among the greatest impossibilities. There is no ground for their wonder at the creation of the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, without a father, for God ﴿creates what He wills﴾: if He wills, from a father and a mother as with the rest of the children of Adam; if He wills, from a father without a mother, as with Eve; if He wills, from a mother without a father, as with Jesus; and if He wills, from neither a father nor a mother, as with Adam. Thus He diversifies His creation by His all-pervading will, to which nothing is unyielding. For this reason He said: ﴿And God is over all things competent.﴾

{18} Among the sayings of the Jews and Christians is that each of them made a false claim by which they praised themselves, saying: ﴿We are the children of God and His beloved.﴾ "Son" in their language means "beloved," and they did not mean literal sonship, for this is not their doctrine, except the Christian doctrine concerning the Messiah. God said, refuting them, since they claimed without proof: ﴿Say: Then why does He punish you for your sins?﴾ If you were His beloved, He would not punish you, because God loves only those who act in accordance with His pleasure. ﴿Rather, you are human beings of those He has created﴾: the rulings of justice and grace apply to you. ﴿He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾ when they bring about causes of forgiveness or causes of punishment. ﴿And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and to Him is the return.﴾ That is: what then has singled you out for this virtue, when you are among the owned, and among those who return to God in the Hereafter, where He will recompense you for your deeds?

{19} Exalted be He, calls the People of the Book, by reason of the favour He has bestowed upon them through His Book, to believe in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and to thank God, who sent him to them {after a gap in the messengers} and at a time of great need for him. This is among the things that call to belief in him, for he makes clear to them all the divine requirements and the legal rulings of the Sharia. God has thereby cut off their argument, lest they say: {There came to us no bringer of good news nor warner. But there has come to you a bringer of good news and a warner.} He gives good news of the reward, both the immediate and the deferred, and of the deeds that merit it and the description of those who perform them; and he warns of the punishment, both the immediate and the deferred, and of the deeds that merit it and the description of those who perform them. {And God is over all things Powerful.} Things submit willingly and humbly to His power, so nothing among them is beyond His control. And of His power is that He sent the messengers and revealed the Books, and that He rewards those who obey them and punishes those who disobey them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 5, verses 33–34:

{33} "Those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger, and strive to cause corruption on earth, shall be put to death, or crucified, or have their hands and feet cut off from opposite sides, or be banished from the land." The ones who wage war against Allah and His Messenger are those who openly oppose them with enmity, and who spread corruption on earth through disbelief, killing, seizing wealth, and terrorizing the roads (al-sabil). It is well known that this noble verse concerns the rulings on highway robbers (qutta' al-tariq), who ambush people in villages and deserts, seize their property, kill them, and terrify them, so that people refrain from traveling the routes they control, and thereby the roads are cut off. Allah informs that their recompense and punishment, when the prescribed penalty (hadd) is carried out upon them, is that one of these matters is done to them.

The exegetes differed as to whether this is at the discretion (al-takhyir) — so that for every highway robber the Imam, or his deputy, does whichever of these matters he deems to be in the public interest — and this is the apparent meaning of the wording; or whether their punishment is according to their crimes, such that every crime has a corresponding portion, as the verse indicates by its wisdom and its agreement with the wisdom of Allah, the Exalted. Accordingly: if they kill and take property, their killing and crucifixion are mandatory, so that they become notorious, are disgraced, and others are deterred; if they kill but do not take property, their killing alone is mandatory; if they take property but do not kill, their hands and feet are mandatorily cut off from opposite sides — the right hand and the left foot; and if they terrify people but neither kill nor take property, they are banished from the land, and they are not left to take shelter in any town until their repentance becomes evident. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) and many of the Imams, with disagreement over some details.

"That" (the punishment) "is a disgrace for them in this world" — that is, shame and disgrace; "and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment." From this it is understood that highway robbery is among the greatest sins, entailing disgrace in this world and punishment in the Hereafter, and that its perpetrator is one who wages war against Allah and His Messenger. Since this is the gravity of this crime, it is known that purifying the earth of corrupters, securing the roads and paths against killing, seizing property, and terrorizing people, is among the greatest good deeds and most exalted acts of obedience, and that it is a reform on earth, just as its opposite is corruption on earth.

{34} "Except for those who repent before you gain power over them" — that is, from among these combatants. "Then know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful" — that is, He drops from them what was due to Allah of mandatory killing, crucifixion, amputation, and banishment, and also the right of the human being, if the combatant was a disbeliever who then embraced Islam. But if the combatant was a Muslim, the right of the human being is not dropped from him, whether it is killing or the seizure of property. The implication of the verse indicates that the repentance of a combatant after he has come under one's power does not drop anything from him. The wisdom in this is evident. And if repentance before one gains power over him prevents the prescribed penalty for highway robbery from being carried out, then for other prescribed penalties, if one repents from committing them before gaining power over him, it is all the more so (min bab awla).

This is a command from Allah to His believing servants to do what faith requires: fear of Allah (taqwa) and caution against His displeasure and anger. This means that the servant should strive and exert his utmost capacity in avoiding what displeases Allah, namely sins of the heart, the tongue, and the outward and inward limbs, and seek Allah's help in abandoning them, so that he may be saved thereby from Allah's displeasure and punishment. ﴿And seek the means of nearness to Him﴾; i.e., nearness to Him, closeness to Him, and love for Him. This is achieved by performing His obligations: the obligations of the heart, such as love for Him and for His sake, fear, hope, turning in repentance (inabah), and reliance (tawakkul); the physical obligations, such as zakah and Hajj; and those combining both, such as prayer (salah) and similar acts such as various kinds of recitation (qira'ah) and remembrance (dhikr); and kinds of benevolence toward creation through wealth, knowledge, standing, body, and sincere counsel to the servants of Allah. All these deeds bring one near to Allah, and the servant continues to draw near to Allah through them until He loves him. When Allah loves him, He becomes his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks, and Allah answers his supplication.

Then, may He be blessed and exalted, singled out from the acts of worship that bring one near to Him, jihad in His cause, which is exerting effort in fighting the disbelievers with wealth, self, opinion, and tongue, and striving to support the religion of Allah with everything the servant is able to do. This is because this kind of act is among the most noble acts of obedience and the best means of drawing near (to Allah), and because whoever performs it is more worthy and more deserving of performing the others. ﴿That you may be successful﴾: if you fear Allah by abandoning sins, seek the means of nearness to Allah by performing acts of obedience, and strive in His cause seeking His pleasure. Falah (success) is attaining and triumphing in every sought-after and desired thing, and being saved from every feared thing; its reality is everlasting happiness and enduring bliss.

{36–37} He, exalted is He, informs of the dreadful state of the disbelievers [in God] on the Day of Resurrection and their terrible end: that even if they were to ransom themselves from the punishment of God with the fill of the earth in gold, and the like of it along with it, it would not be accepted from them nor would it benefit them, because the place of ransom has passed and there remains only the painful, agonizing, everlasting punishment from which they will never come out, but rather they will remain in it forever.

{38} The thief (al-sariq) is one who takes the property of another that is protected (al-muhtaram) secretly and without the owner's consent. It is among the major sins (kaba'ir al-dhunub) that entail the imposition of a grievous punishment, namely the cutting off of the right hand, as is found in the recitation of some of the Companions. The limit of the hand, when stated without qualification, is from the wrist (al-kva'). So if a person steals, his hand is cut off at the wrist and the stump is sealed in oil so that the veins are closed and the blood stops. However, the Sunnah has restricted the generality of this verse in several respects. Among them is the requirement of a secured place (hirz): the theft must be from a secured place, and the secured place for each property is that in which it is customarily kept. So if one steals from a place that is not secured, there is no amputation upon him. Among them is also that the stolen property must reach the minimum value (nisab), which is a quarter of a dinar or three dirhams, or what is worth one of them. So if he steals less than that, there is no amputation upon him. This may perhaps be derived from the word "theft" (al-sariqah) and its meaning, for the word "theft" means taking a thing in a manner that cannot be guarded against, and that requires that the property be secured; so if it is not secured, that does not constitute legal theft (sariqah shar'iyyah).

It is also part of the wisdom that the hand not be cut off for a trivial and worthless thing. Since a measure was necessary, the legal measure became a specifier of the Book. The wisdom in cutting off the hand for theft is that this preserves property and safeguards it, and that the limb from which the offence proceeded be cut off. If the thief returns (to theft), his left foot is cut off. If he returns again, it is said: his left hand is cut off, then his right foot. And it is said: he is imprisoned until he dies.

His saying: {as a recompense for what they committed} means: that cutting is a recompense for the thief for what he stole from the wealth of people. {as an exemplary punishment from Allah} means: a deterrent and a warning to the thief and to others, so that thieves may be restrained when they know that they will be cut off if they steal. {And Allah is Mighty and Wise} means: He is Mighty and He judges, so He cut off the thief.

Ibn Sa'di discusses the Jews who listen to lies and follow their leaders, who say "If you are given this, take it; if not, beware," and he explains that the one who seeks a ruling only to satisfy his desires shows an impure heart, while one who accepts the Shari'ah ruling whether or not it suits him shows a pure heart.

On verse 42, the commentator notes that the Prophet was given the choice to judge between them or to turn away, and that if he judges, he must judge justly, since God loves the just. On verses 43–44, he observes that the Jews who turned away from the Torah are not believers, that the Torah contains guidance and light, and that the prophets and rabbis judged by it. He explains that scholars bear a responsibility to teach and must not fear people over God, and that not judging by what God revealed is disbelief, which may be major disbelief if one considers it lawful, or a grave sin otherwise.

This ruling is among the rulings contained in the Torah, by which the prophets who submitted (aslamu) judged for those who were Jews (alladhina hadu), as did the rabbis (al-rabbaniyyun) and the scholars (al-ahbar). For Allah obligated upon them that a soul which kills is to be killed in return for the soul, on condition of intent (al-amd) and equivalence (al-mukafa'ah), and the eye is to be taken out in return for the eye, the ear is to be taken in return for the ear, and the tooth is to be pulled out in return for the tooth. Similar to these, and what resembles them, are the limbs which retaliation can be carried out upon without injustice.

{And for wounds, retaliation}: Retaliation (al-iqtisas) means that the same is done to him as he did. So whoever wounds another intentionally, retribution is taken from the wounder by a wound like his wound, in its type (haddan), its place, its length, its breadth and its depth.

It should be known that the law of those before us is law for us, so long as our law does not reveal something contrary to it. {But whoever forgoes it}: that is, forgoes retaliation for the soul and what is less than it of limbs and wounds, by pardoning the one who committed the offence while the right against him is established. {It is an expiation for him}: that is, an expiation for the offender, because the human has pardoned his right, and Allah, the Exalted, is more entitled and more worthy to pardon His right. It is also an expiation for the one who pardons, for just as he pardons the one who wronged him or someone connected to him, Allah pardons his lapses and offences. {And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, then those are the wrongdoers}: Ibn 'Abbas said: it is disbelief less than disbelief, wrongdoing less than wrongdoing, and sinfulness less than sinfulness. So it is a greater wrongdoing if he deems it lawful, and a great and grave matter if he does it while not deeming it lawful.

{48} God, exalted is He, says: {And We have sent down to you the Book} — which is the Great Qur'an, the best and most honoured of books — {in truth}; that is, sent down in truth, and comprising truth in its reports, its commands and its prohibitions. {Confirming what came before it of the Scripture} — because it bears witness to them, agrees with them, its reports correspond to their reports, its major laws correspond to their laws, and they gave news of it, so that its existence became a confirmation of their report. {And a criterion over it} — that is, it comprises what the previous books comprised, plus an increase in divine matters and in the moral qualities of the soul. Otherwise, had it been from God, it would not have contradicted it. {So judge between them by what God has revealed} — from the lawful judgment that God has revealed to you. {And do not follow their desires, diverting from what has come to you of the truth} — that is, do not make the following of their corrupt desires, which oppose the truth, a substitute for what has come to you of the truth, lest you exchange what is lower for what is better.

To each of you, O nations, We have made {a law and a way} — that is, a path and a practice. These laws, which differ according to the nations, are the ones that change according to the change of times and circumstances, and all of them return to justice at the time of their enactment. As for the great foundations, which are a benefit and a wisdom in every age, they do not differ, so they are enacted in all laws. {And had God willed, He would have made you one nation} — following one law, whose later and earlier do not differ. {But He might test you in what He has given you} — so that He may examine you and see how you act, and try each nation according to what His wisdom requires, giving each one what suits it, and so that competition arises among the nations, each one eager to outstrip the others. For this reason He said: {So race to [all] good deeds} — that is, hasten to them and perfect them, for the good deeds, which include every obligatory and recommended act relating to the rights of God and the rights of His servants, do not make their doer one who precedes others and gains command except by two things: hastening to them, and seizing the opportunity when its time comes and its occasion presents itself, and striving to perform them completely in the manner commanded.

{49} {And judge between them by what God has revealed}: This verse is the one said to abrogate His saying: {So judge between them, or turn away from them}. {51} God, exalted is He, guides His servant-believers, when He has explained to them the conditions and the unpraiseworthy attributes of the Jews and the Christians, that they should not take them as allies (awliya'). For some of them are {allies of one another}: they support one another among themselves, and they are a single hand against others. So you should not take them as allies, for they are the enemies in truth. They do not care about your harm; rather, they spare no effort in misguiding you. Therefore, none takes them as allies except one who is like them. This is why He said: ﴿And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed he is one of them﴾, because full alliance necessitates transferring to their religion, and a little alliance calls to much of it, and then it progresses little by little until the servant becomes one of them. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾; that is, those whose description is wrongdoing (zulm), and to Him they will return, and upon Him they rely. So even if you brought them every sign, they would not follow you, nor would they submit to you.

{52} When God forbade the believers from allying with them, He informed that among those who claim faith there is a group who ally with them. So He said: ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾; that is, doubt, hypocrisy, and weakness of faith. They say: "Our alliance with them is out of need, for indeed we fear that a misfortune (da'irah) may befall us"; that is, that the turn of fortune (ad-da'irah) would be for the Jews and the Christians. So if fortune were to be theirs, then they would have a hand with them that would reward them for it. This is an evil assumption on their part about Islam. God, exalted is He, said, refuting their evil assumption: ﴿Then perhaps Allah will bring a conquest﴾: by which Allah will exalt Islam over the Jews and the Christians, and the Muslims will subdue them; ﴿or a decision from Him﴾: by which the hypocrites will despair of the victory of the disbelievers among the Jews and others; ﴿so they will become, over what they concealed within themselves,﴾; that is, what they harbored ﴿regretful﴾: over what had come from them, and the harm they incurred without any benefit gained. Then the conquest came, by which Allah gave victory to Islam and the Muslims, and humiliated disbelief and the disbelievers. So they regretted, and there befell them such grief as only Allah knows.
