Then the conquest came, by which Allah gave victory to Islam and the Muslims, and humiliated disbelief and the disbelievers. So they regretted, and there befell them such grief as only Allah knows.

{53} ﴿And those who believe will say﴾, marveling at the state of those in whose hearts is a disease: ﴿"Are these the ones who swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that they are with you?"﴾; that is, they swore and confirmed their oath and emphasized it with every kind of emphasis that they were with you in faith and what it necessitates of support, love, and loyalty. What they harbored became apparent, and what they concealed became clear, and their scheming that they schemed and their assumption that they assumed about Islam and its people became void. Their scheming was nullified, and {their deeds}, in this world, were rendered void, ﴿so they became losers﴾, for their aim escaped them, and wretchedness and punishment were brought upon them.

{54} He, exalted is He, informs that He is free of need of the worlds, and that whoever apostatizes from His religion, then he will not harm God at all; he only harms himself. He also informs that God has servants who are sincere and men who are truthful, whom the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, has undertaken to guide and has promised to bring forth. They are the most perfect of creation in attributes, the strongest of souls, and the best of them in character:

The most sublime of their attributes is that God {loves them and they love Him}. For God's love for the servant is the most sublime blessing He bestows upon him and the greatest virtue with which God graces him. When God loves a servant, He facilitates for him the means, makes every difficulty easy for him, enables him to do good and abstain from wrongdoing, and turns the hearts of His servants toward him with love and affection. Among the necessary consequences of the servant's love for his Lord is that he must necessarily characterize himself by following the Messenger (ﷺ), outwardly and inwardly, in his sayings, his deeds, and all his conditions; as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: If you love God, then follow me; God will love you﴾. Likewise, among the necessary consequences of God's love for the servant is that the servant should increase his drawing near to God through obligatory and voluntary acts of worship; as the Prophet (ﷺ) said in the sound hadith, relating from God: "My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him. And My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him; and when I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him; and if he seeks refuge in Me, I will surely grant him refuge."

Among the necessary consequences of the love of God is knowing Him, the Exalted, and frequently remembering Him; for love without knowledge of God is very deficient, indeed non-existent, even if its claim is made. Whoever loves God remembers Him much. And when God loves a servant, He accepts from him little deed and forgives him many faults.

Among their attributes is that they are: ﴿humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers﴾. They are humble toward the believers out of their love for them, their advice to them, their gentleness, their kindness, their mercy, their compassion, their approachability, and the readiness with which they fulfill what is asked of them. And they are mighty against the disbelievers in God who oppose His signs and deny His messengers; their resolve and determination are united in opposing them, and they exert their utmost effort in every means by which victory over them may be achieved. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war, by which you may strike fear into the enemy of God and your enemy﴾. And God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾. Thus, severity against the enemies of God is among what brings the servant closer to God and conforms the servant to his Lord in His wrath against them. Severity and firmness against them do not prevent calling them to the Islamic religion "in the best manner"; so severity and gentleness are combined in calling them, and both matters are for their benefit, and its benefit returns to them.

﴿They strive in the way of God﴾: with their wealth, their selves, their words, and their deeds. ﴿And they do not fear the blame of any blamer﴾: rather, they prefer the pleasure of their Lord and fear of His blame over the blame of creatures. This indicates the strength of their resolve and determination; for the one weak of heart and weak of resolve, his determination collapses at the blame of blamers, and his strength wanes at the rebuke of those who rebuke. In their hearts there is no servitude to other than God to the degree that they consider the creation and prefer their approval and blame over the command of God; the heart is not free of servitude to other than God until one does not fear the blame of any blamer in the cause of God.

When God praised them for the beautiful attributes and lofty virtues He had bestowed upon them, which imply other good deeds not mentioned, He informed that this is from His bounty and beneficence toward them, so that they would not be self-admiring, and that they would thank the One who bestowed this upon them, so that He would increase them from His bounty, and so that others would know that God's bounty is not veiled. So He said: ﴿That is the bounty of God; He gives it to whom He wills, and God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾; meaning: vast in bounty and beneficence, abundant in favors, whose mercy has encompassed everything. He widens for His friends from His bounty what is not given to others; yet He is All-Knowing of who deserves the bounty, so He gives it to him. God knows best where He places His message, in its root and its branches.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 5, verses 55–56:

{55} When He had forbidden taking as allies the disbelievers from among the Jews, the Christians and others, and mentioned that the outcome of taking them as allies is manifest loss, Allah, exalted is He, informed of those whose allegiance is obligatory and required, and mentioned the benefit and the good of that. He said: ﴿Your only ally is Allah, and His Messenger, and those who believe﴾. The allegiance of Allah is attained through faith and piety; so everyone who is a believer and pious is an ally of Allah. Whoever is an ally of Allah is also an ally of His Messenger. And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger as allies, the completion of that is to take as allies those whom they have taken as allies, namely the believers who uphold faith outwardly and inwardly, and who are sincere to the One worshipped by establishing the prayer with its conditions, its obligations and its complements, who do good to creation, and who give the zakah from their wealth to those among them who are entitled to it. His words ﴿and they bow down [in prayer]﴾ mean: they are humbly submissive and abased before Allah. The particle of restriction in His words ﴿Your only ally is Allah, and His Messenger, and those who believe﴾ indicates that it is obligatory to restrict allegiance to those mentioned and to disassociate from the allegiance of others.

{56} Then He mentioned the benefit of this allegiance, saying: ﴿And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies, then indeed the party of Allah, they are the victorious﴾. That is: he is among the party attributed to Allah by the attribution of servitude and allegiance, and His party are the victorious, who have the final outcome in this world and the Hereafter; as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And indeed Our soldiers, they will be the victorious﴾. This is a great good tiding for whoever stands up for the command of Allah and becomes of His party and His soldiers, that for him is victory, even if he is overcome at certain times for a wisdom that Allah intends; so the end of his affair is triumph and victory. And who is more truthful than Allah in speech?

{57-58} He forbids His believing servants from taking the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, and all the other disbelievers, as allies (awliya'), those who love them and befriend them, reveal to them the secrets of the believers, and assist them in some of their affairs that harm Islam and the Muslims. And the faith that is with them obliges them to abandon allegiance to them and urges them to be hostile to them. Likewise, their adherence to taqwa of Allah, which is carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, calls them to be hostile to them. Likewise, [He forbids them from emulating] what the polytheists and the disbelievers who oppose the Muslims did: disparaging the religion of the Muslims, taking it in mockery and play, and belittling and despising it, especially the prayer, which is the most manifest of the symbols of the Muslims and the most noble of their acts of worship. When they call to it, they take it in mockery and play. This is due to their lack of intellect and their great ignorance. Otherwise, if they had intellects, they would submit to it and would know that it is greater than all the virtues with which souls are characterized. So, O believers, when you know the condition of the disbelievers and the intensity of their hostility toward you and your religion, whoever does not oppose them after this shows that Islam is cheap in his sight, that he does not care about whoever disparages it or disparages it with disbelief and misguidance, and that he has no manliness or humanity whatsoever. How, then, can you claim for yourself a upright religion, and that it is the true religion and that whatever else is false, and yet be content with allying with those who have taken it in mockery and play, and mocked it and its people, from among the people of ignorance and folly?! And this contains, in terms of stirring up enmity toward them, what is known to everyone who has the least understanding.

{63} {Why do the rabbis and scholars not forbid them from their sinful speech and their consuming of the unlawful?}; that is: Why do not the scholars, who take on the task of benefiting people, upon whom God has bestowed knowledge and wisdom, forbid them from the sins that issue from them, so that the ignorance they have may be removed and God's proof established against them? For scholars are responsible for commanding people to good and forbidding them from evil, and for clarifying for them the lawful path, encouraging them toward good and warning them against evil. {Wretched is what they have been doing}.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 5, verses 64–66:**

{64} Allah, exalted is He, informs us of the abominable statement of the Jews and their dreadful belief. He says: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Hand of Allah is chained up."﴾ That is, (He is withholding) from goodness, benevolence and righteousness! ﴿Their hands are chained up, and they are cursed for what they said.﴾ This is a supplication against them with the same kind of statement they made, for their words imply describing the Generous Lord with stinginess and failure to show kindness. So He repaid them by making this attribute apply to themselves. They became the most miserly of people, the least of them in kindness, the worst in their opinion of Allah, and the farthest from His mercy, which encompasses all things and fills the regions of the upper and lower worlds. Therefore He said: ﴿Rather, His hands are both outstretched; He spends as He wills.﴾ There is no restriction upon Him, and nothing prevents Him from what He wills. Indeed, He, exalted is He, has spread out His religious and worldly bounty and His kindness, and He commanded His servants to seek the breezes of His generosity and not to close off for themselves the doors of His benevolence through their disobedience. His hand pours out by night and day, and His goodness flows at all times. He relieves distress, removes grief, enriches the poor, frees the captive, mends the broken, answers the petitioner, gives to the destitute who has dependents, responds to the desperate, answers those who ask, bestows favor upon those who do not ask Him, grants well-being to those who seek it, and does not withhold His goodness from the disobedient. Rather, the righteous and the wicked both partake of His goodness. He bestows upon His allies the success to perform righteous deeds, then praises them for them and attributes them to them, though they are from His generosity, and He rewards them for them with a reward, both immediate and deferred, that description cannot encompass and that does not occur to the mind of the servant. He is gentle with them in all their affairs, brings to them benevolence, and averts from them calamities of which they are largely unaware. Glory be to Him, from whom come all the blessings that are among the servants, and to whom they turn in supplication to repel hardships. Blessed is He whom no one can enumerate His praise, rather He is as He praised Himself. Exalted is He, from whose generosity the servants are not free for the blink of an eye; indeed, they have no existence and no continuance except by His generosity. May Allah disfigure the one who considers himself independent of his Lord through his ignorance and attributes to Him what is not befitting His majesty. Indeed, if Allah were to deal with the Jews who uttered that statement, and others like them whose condition is like theirs, according to some of their words, they would perish and be wretched in their worldly life. But they say those statements, and He, exalted is He, is forbearing toward them, forgiving, and gives them respite; He does not neglect them.
And His saying: ﴿But surely what has been sent down to you from your Lord will increase many of them in rebellion and disbelief.﴾ This is among the greatest of punishments upon a servant: that the Reminder which Allah sent down to His Messenger, in which is the life of the heart and the soul, the happiness of this world and the Hereafter, and the success of both abodes, which is the greatest favor Allah has bestowed upon His servants and which requires them to hasten to accept it, submit to Allah through it, and give thanks to Allah for it, should instead increase such people in their error, their rebellion and their disbelief. This is because of their turning away from it, rejecting it, opposing it, and contesting it with false doubts. ﴿And We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection.﴾ So they do not come together, do not support one another, and do not agree upon any condition in which their interest lies. Rather, they have continued to harbor hatred in their hearts and enmity in their actions until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Every time they kindle a fire for war,﴾ to plot thereby against Islam and its people, ﴿Allah extinguishes it,﴾ through their abandonment, the scattering of their armies, and the victory of the Muslims over them. ﴿And they strive upon the earth to cause corruption,﴾ that is, they exert effort and strive, but for corruption upon the earth, by committing sins, calling to their false religion, and hindering others from entering Islam. ﴿And Allah does not love the corrupters.﴾ Rather, He hates them with the utmost hatred, and He will requite them for that.

{65} Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if the People of the Book had believed and feared Allah, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them into Gardens of Pleasure.﴾ This is from His generosity and benevolence. Having mentioned the ugly deeds, defects and false statements of the People of the Book, He called them to repentance, and informed them that if they believed in Allah, His angels, all His books and all His messengers, and feared Allah by avoiding sins, He would remove their misdeeds, however great they were, and would admit them into the Gardens of Pleasure, in which is what the souls desire and what delights the eyes.

{66} ﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was sent down to them from their Lord﴾: that is, had they carried out their commands [and prohibitions] as Allah urged and exhorted them to do. Among upholding them is belief in what they called to, namely belief in Muhammad (ﷺ) and in the Qur'an. So if they had observed this great blessing which their Lord sent down to them, that is, for their sake and for their benefit, ﴿they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet.﴾ That is, Allah would have made provision abundant for them, sent rain from the sky upon them, and made the earth bring forth for them, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and feared Allah, We would have opened upon them blessings from the sky and the earth.﴾ ﴿Among them﴾, that is, among the People of the Book, ﴿is a moderate community﴾, that is, acting upon the Torah and the Gospel with action that is neither strong nor energetic. ﴿But many of them—evil is what they do.﴾ That is, the majority of them are evildoers, and as for the foremost among them, they are few.

This is a command from God to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) concerning the greatest and most magnificent of commands, which is the conveying (al-tabligh) of what God has sent down to him. This includes every matter that the Ummah received from him (ﷺ) regarding beliefs (al-aqa'id), actions (al-a'mal), statements (al-aqwal), legal rulings (al-ahkam al-shar'iyyah), and divine requirements (al-matalib al-ilahiyyah). He (ﷺ) conveyed in the most complete manner; he called, warned, gave glad tidings, and made things easy, and he taught the unlettered ignorant until they became among the divine scholars (al-ulama al-rabbaniyyun). He conveyed by his speech, his deeds, his writings, and his messengers, so no good was left without his directing his Ummah to it, and no evil was left without his warning them against it. The best of the Ummah testified to his conveying: the Companions, then those who followed them, the imams of the religion and the men of the Muslims.

{And if you do not}; that is: if you do not convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord, {then you have not conveyed His message}; that is: then you have not carried out His command. {And God will protect you from the people}: this is protection and safeguarding from God for His Messenger from the people. It means that your eagerness should be for teaching and conveying, and fear of created beings should not turn you away from it, for their forelocks are in the hand of God, and He has undertaken to safeguard you. You are only responsible for the clear conveyance. Whoever is guided, it is for his own soul; as for the disbelievers, whose only aim is to follow their desires, God does not guide them, and does not grant them success in good because of their disbelief.

{68} That is: say to the People of the Book, proclaiming their misguidance and openly declaring their falsehood: {You stand on nothing} of religious matters; for you have believed neither in the Qur'an nor in Muhammad, you have not affirmed your own Prophet and your own Book, you have not held fast to any truth, and you have not relied upon any foundation. {Until you establish the Torah and the Gospel}; that is, make them standing by believing in them, following them, and holding fast to everything they call to. {And} establish {what has been revealed to you from your Lord}, the One who nurtured you and bestowed His favour upon you, and whose greatest favour was the sending down of Books to you. It is therefore obligatory upon you to give thanks to God, to adhere to the rulings of God, and to uphold what you have been entrusted with of God's trust and covenant. {And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in rebellion and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.}

{69} Almighty God informs us that the People of the Book, meaning those of the Qur'an, the Torah and the Gospel, have their happiness and salvation in one path and one root, which is faith in God and the Last Day together with righteous deeds. Whoever among them believes in God and the Last Day and does righteous deeds, for him is salvation, and there is no fear upon them regarding what they face of frightening matters, nor will they grieve over what they have left behind. This ruling mentioned here encompasses all times.

**(70)** He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, We took the covenant of the Children of Israel﴾, that is, their weighty pledge to believe in Allah and to fulfill the duties discussed earlier in His words: ﴿And Allah had already taken the covenant of the Children of Israel, and We raised up among them twelve leaders...﴾ to the end of the verses. ﴿And We sent to them messengers﴾, who followed one another in calling them and in guiding them with counsel. But that did not benefit them or have any effect on them. ﴿Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire﴾ of the truth, they denied him, opposed him, and treated him in the vilest manner, ﴿a party they denied and a party they killed﴾.

**(71)** ﴿And they thought there would be no trial﴾, that is, they supposed that their disobedience and their denial would bring upon them no punishment or retribution. They persisted in their falsehood and were blind ﴿and deaf﴾ to the truth. ﴿Then﴾ He raised them up, ﴿and Allah turned to them﴾ when they repented and turned back to Him. ﴿Then﴾ they did not persist in that, until most of them reverted to the vile state; so ﴿they became blind and deaf, many of them﴾ with this description. A few persisted in their repentance and faith. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾: He will repay every doer for his deed, good with good and evil with evil.

{72} He, may He be exalted, informs about the disbelief of the Christians in their saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary﴾, on the basis of the doubt that he came forth from a mother without a father, contrary to the customary divine creation. Yet the Messiah, peace be upon him, had already denied their claim and said to them: ﴿O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord﴾. Thus he affirmed for himself complete servitude and for his Lord the all-encompassing lordship over every creature. ﴿Indeed, whoever associates with Allah﴾ anyone among the creatures, neither Jesus nor other than him, ﴿Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire﴾. This is because he equated the created with the Creator and directed to other than its rightful recipient the pure worship that Allah created for Him alone; therefore he deserves to abide forever in the Fire. ﴿And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers﴾: no one who can rescue them from the punishment of Allah or repel from them some of what has descended upon them.

{73} ﴿Surely those who say, "Allah is the third of three," have disbelieved﴾. This is among the sayings of the Christians that are famous among them. They claim that Allah is the third of three: Allah, Jesus, and Mary! Exalted is Allah far above what they say, a great exaltation. This is the greatest proof of the feeble intellect of the Christians: how did they accept this abominable saying and this ugly belief? How did the Creator become confused with the created for them? How was the Lord of the worlds hidden from them? Allah, the Exalted, responded to them and to those like them: ﴿There is no god except one God﴾, endowed with every attribute of perfection, free from every deficiency, singular in creating and governing, with no blessing among creatures except from Him. How, then, could another god be made along with Him? Exalted is Allah far above what the wrongdoers say, a great exaltation. Then He threatened them with His saying: ﴿And if they do not desist from what they say, a painful punishment will surely afflict those among them who disbelieve.﴾

{74} Then He called them to repent from what they had committed, and made clear that He accepts repentance from His servants. He said: ﴿Will they not turn in repentance to Allah?﴾; that is, will they not return to what He loves and is pleased with, namely acknowledging Allah's oneness and that Jesus is the servant and messenger of Allah, and [turn away from] what they used to say, ﴿and seek His forgiveness﴾ for what they had committed. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾; that is, He forgives the sins of those who repent, even if they reach the sky, and shows mercy to them by accepting their repentance and changing their evil deeds into good deeds. He introduced His call to repentance with the gentle and soft manner that is at the utmost of kindness and tenderness in His saying: ﴿Will they not turn in repentance to Allah?﴾

{75} Then He mentioned the true reality of the Messiah and his mother, which is the truth, and said: ﴿The Messiah, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger; messengers had passed away before him﴾; that is, this is his limit and the end of his station: he is one of the servants of Allah, the messengers, who have no authority or legislation except what Allah has sent them with. He is of the same kind as the messengers before him, and he has no distinction over them that would lift him out of humanity to the rank of lordship. ﴿And his mother [Mary] was a truthful woman﴾; that is, this too is the limit of her station: she was among the ṣiddīqūn (the truthful), who are the highest of creation in rank after the prophets. Ṣiddīqiyyah is beneficial knowledge that yields certainty and righteous action. This is evidence that Mary was not a prophetess; rather, the highest of her conditions was ṣiddīqiyyah, and that is sufficient as virtue and honor. Likewise, none of the women was a prophetess, because Allah placed prophethood in the more perfect of the two kinds, men, as He said: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed﴾. So if Jesus, peace be upon him, is of the same kind as the prophets and messengers before him, and his mother is a truthful woman, then for what reason did the Christians take them both as gods besides Allah?

And His saying: ﴿They both used to eat food﴾ is a clear proof that they were two servants, poor and needy, who need food and drink as the children of Adam do. Had they been gods, they would have been independent of food and drink and in need of nothing, for the god is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy. When Allah had made the proof clear, He said: ﴿Look how We make the signs clear to them﴾, the signs that clarify the truth and reveal certainty; yet despite this they benefit nothing among them, and they continue in their falsehood, lying, and fabrication. That is wrongdoing and obstinacy on their part.

Ibn Sa'di's commentary on Surah al-Ma'idah (5), verses 77–81:

{77} Allah says to His Prophet (ﷺ): {Say: "O People of the Scripture, do not exceed the bounds in your religion, going beyond the truth."} That is: do not overstep, nor transgress from the truth into falsehood. This is like their saying about the Messiah what was previously related of them, and like their exaggeration regarding some shaykhs, following their whims. {A people who had strayed before} — that is, whose misguidance had already preceded — {and had led many astray} — by calling people to the religion they themselves adhered to — {and had strayed from the right way}, that is, from the straight path. Thus they combined going astray with leading others astray. These are the leaders of misguidance, against whom Allah warned, and against following their ruinous whims and their misguiding opinions.

{78} Then Allah says: {Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel} — that is, they were expelled and removed from the mercy of Allah — {upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary} — that is, by their testimony and affirmation that the proof had been established against them and that they had obstinately opposed it. {That} — the disbelief and the curse — {is because they disobeyed and used to transgress}; that is, their disobedience to Allah and their wronging of the servants of Allah became a cause of their disbelief and their distance from the mercy of Allah, for sins and wrongdoing have their consequences.

{79} And among their sins that brought upon them calamities and inflicted punishments was that {they did not forbid one another from wrongdoing that they committed}; that is, they used to commit wrongdoing and did not forbid one another. Thereby both the perpetrator and others who remained silent about forbidding wrong, while being able to do so, share in the guilt. This indicates their negligence regarding the command of Allah and that disobedience to Him was light upon them. Had they held their Lord in reverence, they would have been jealous for His prohibitions and angered by His anger.
Silence about wrongdoing while able to prevent it is only deserving of punishment because of the great corruptions it entails:
Among them: mere silence is itself an act of disobedience, even if the silent person does not commit the sin himself; for just as it is obligatory to avoid sin, it is obligatory to denounce the one who commits it.
Among them: as previously mentioned, it indicates negligence toward sins and little concern for them.
Among them: it emboldens sinners and wrongdoers to multiply their sins when they are not restrained, so evil increases and the religious and worldly calamity grows, they gain power and prominence, and then the people of goodness grow too weak to resist the people of evil, until they can no longer do what they were once able to do.
Among them: in abandoning the denunciation of wrong, knowledge is effaced and ignorance multiplies; for sin, when repeated and committed by many persons while the people of religion and knowledge do not denounce it, is thought not to be sin, and the ignorant may even think it a commendable act of worship. And what corruption is greater than believing what Allah has forbidden to be lawful, the reversal of realities in souls, and seeing falsehood as truth?
Among them: silence toward the disobedience of the disobedient may cause sin to appear attractive in people's hearts, and some follow others, for a person is inclined to imitate his peers and kind... and [other reasons]...
Since silence from denunciation is of this standing, Allah stated that the disbelieving Children of Israel were cursed by Him for their sins and transgression, and He singled out this great wrong: {Evil indeed was what they used to do.}

{80} {You see many of them taking as allies those who disbelieve} — through love, alliance, and support. {Evil is what their souls have put forward for them} — this [is] the worthless merchandise and the losing bargain, namely the wrath of Allah, by which everything is angered, and eternal abiding in the great punishment. Their souls wronged them, for they sent ahead for themselves this ignoble abode, and they also wronged themselves by forfeiting for themselves the lasting bliss.

{81} {If they had believed in Allah, the Prophet, and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies}. Indeed, faith in Allah, His Prophet, and what was revealed to him requires of the servant that he take his Lord as ally, take His allies as allies, and oppose those who disbelieve in Him, oppose Him, and persist in disobeying Him. The condition of the wilayah of Allah and of faith in Him is that one not take the enemies of Allah as allies; these people did not fulfil this condition, which indicates the absence of what is conditioned. {But many of them are defiant} — that is, they have departed from obedience to Allah and from faith in Him and in the Prophet; and among their defiance is their alliance with the enemies of Allah.

Ibn Sa'di's commentary on Surah al-Ma'idah (5), verses 77–81:

This is like their saying about the Messiah what was previously related of them, and like their exaggeration regarding some shaykhs, following their whims. {A people who had strayed before} — that is, whose misguidance had already preceded — {and had led many astray} — by calling people to the religion they themselves adhered to — {and had strayed from the right way}, that is, from the straight path. Thus they combined going astray with leading others astray. These are the leaders of misguidance, against whom Allah warned, and against following their ruinous whims and their misguiding opinions.

{78} Then Allah says: {Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel} — that is, they were expelled and removed from the mercy of Allah — {upon the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary} — that is, by their testimony and affirmation that the proof had been established against them and that they had obstinately opposed it. {That} — the disbelief and the curse — {is because they disobeyed and used to transgress}; that is, their disobedience to Allah and their wronging of the servants of Allah became a cause of their disbelief and their distance from the mercy of Allah, for sins and wrongdoing have their consequences.

{79} And among their sins that brought upon them calamities and inflicted punishments was that {they did not forbid one another from wrongdoing that they committed}; that is, they used to commit wrongdoing and did not forbid one another. Thereby both the perpetrator and others who remained silent about forbidding wrong, while being able to do so, share in the guilt. This indicates their negligence regarding the command of Allah and that disobedience to Him was light upon them. Had they held their Lord in reverence, they would have been jealous for His prohibitions and angered by His anger.

Among them: mere silence is itself an act of disobedience, even if the silent person does not commit the sin himself; for just as it is obligatory to avoid sin, it is obligatory to denounce the one who commits it.
Among them: as previously mentioned, it indicates negligence toward sins and little concern for them.
Among them: it emboldens sinners and wrongdoers to multiply their sins when they are not restrained, so evil increases and the religious and worldly calamity grows, they gain power and prominence, and then the people of goodness grow too weak to resist the people of evil, until they can no longer do what they were once able to do.
Among them: in abandoning the denunciation of wrong, knowledge is effaced and ignorance multiplies; for sin, when repeated and committed by many persons while the people of religion and knowledge do not denounce it, is thought not to be sin, and the ignorant may even think it a commendable act of worship. And what corruption is greater than believing what Allah has forbidden to be lawful, the reversal of realities in souls, and seeing falsehood as truth?

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 5, verses 82–86:

{82} Allah, exalted is He, states, in clarifying which of the two groups is closest to the Muslims, to their guardianship and to their love, and which is furthest from that: {You will certainly find the most intense of the people in enmity toward those who believe to be the Jews and those who associate others with Allah}. These two groups, absolutely, are the greatest of people in opposition to Islam and the Muslims, and the most eager among them to inflict harm upon them, due to their intense hatred for them, out of transgression, envy, obstinacy and disbelief. {And you will find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe to be those who say, "We are Christians"}. Allah, exalted is He, mentioned several reasons for this:
Among them: that among them are {priests and monks}; that is, scholars who are ascetic and worshippers who devote themselves in monasteries. Knowledge together with asceticism, and likewise worship, are things that soften the heart, make it tender, and remove from it the harshness and roughness it may contain; therefore one does not find among them the harshness of the Jews or the severity of the polytheists.
Among them: {that they are not arrogant}; that is, there is among them no haughtiness nor refusal to submit to the truth. This necessitates their nearness to the Muslims and their love for them, for the humble is closer to goodness than the arrogant.

{83} Among them: that {when they hear what has been revealed} to Muhammad (ﷺ), it affects their hearts, they humble themselves before it, and their eyes overflow with tears according to what they hear of the truth which they have become certain of; therefore they believed and acknowledged it, and they said: {Our Lord, we have believed, so write us among the witnesses}. They are the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ), who bear witness to Allah's oneness, to His messengers' prophethood and the soundness of what they brought, and who bear witness against the previous nations regarding their affirmation and denial; they are upright, and their testimony is accepted, as Allah, exalted is He, said: {And thus We have made you a justly balanced nation that you may be witnesses over mankind and the Messenger may be a witness over you}.

{84} It is as if they were blamed for their faith and their hastening toward it, so they said: {And what is [the matter] with us that we should not believe in Allah and what has come to us of the truth, while we aspire that our Lord will admit us [to Paradise] with the righteous people?}; that is: what prevents us from believing in Allah, when the truth has come to us from our Lord, which admits of no doubt or uncertainty? And if we believe and follow the truth, we hope that Allah will admit us to Paradise with the righteous people. So what prevents us? Does this not necessitate hastening and submitting to faith and not lagging behind it?

{85} Allah, exalted is He, said: {So Allah rewarded them for what they said}; that is, for what they uttered of faith and articulated of affirmation of the truth: {gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein; and that is the reward of the doers of good}. These verses were revealed concerning the Christians who believed in Muhammad (ﷺ), such as the Negus and others among them who believed. Likewise, there continue to be among them those who choose the religion of Islam, and the falsehood of what they were upon becomes clear to them; and they are closer than the Jews and the polytheists to the religion of Islam.

{86} When He mentioned the reward of the doers of good, He mentioned the punishment of the evildoers, saying: {But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs – those are the companions of Hellfire}; because they disbelieved in Allah and denied His signs that make the truth clear.

{87} God, exalted is He, says: "O you who have believed, do not forbid the good things which Allah has made lawful for you" — [this refers to] foods and drinks, for they are blessings which Allah has bestowed upon you. So praise Him for making them lawful for you, and give thanks to Him, and do not repay His blessing with disbelief in it, or with refusing it, or with believing it to be forbidden. By doing so you would combine two things: uttering a lie against Allah, and ungratefulness for the blessing, and holding the lawful good to be unlawful and defiled. This is transgression, and Allah has forbidden transgression, saying: "And do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors" — rather, He hates them, detests them, and punishes them for it.

{88} Then He commanded the opposite of what the polytheists practice, those who forbid what Allah has made lawful, saying: "And eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good." That is: eat from His provision which He has brought to you through the means He has facilitated, provided it is lawful, not by theft, usurpation, or any other kind of wealth taken without right, and also good, meaning that which contains no defilement. Thereby the vile is excluded, such as predatory animals and other impure things. "And fear Allah" — in carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions — "in whom you are believers." Indeed, your belief in Allah obligates you to be mindful of Him and to observe His right, for faith is not complete without that.

The noble verse indicates that if a person makes unlawful for himself something lawful, such as food, drink, a concubine, a slave-woman, or the like, it does not become unlawful by his prohibition; however, if he does it, he must make expiation for an oath, as Allah, exalted is He, said: "O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you...?" [the verse]. Except that prohibiting a wife carries the expiation of zihar. This verse also includes that a person should not avoid the good things and deprive himself of them, but rather partake of them, seeking help through them in obedience to his Lord.

[the verse]. Except that prohibiting a wife carries the expiation of zihar. {89} That is, [the expiation is due] for your oaths that were uttered as mere idle talk (laghw), which are oaths sworn by the one swearing without intention or purpose, or oaths he concluded believing his own statement to be true, but it turned out otherwise. {But He will hold you accountable for the oaths you have sworn firmly}; that is, for what you resolved upon and what your hearts were set upon, as He said in the other verse: {But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned}. {Its expiation} – that is, the expiation for the oath you have sworn with deliberate intent – {is the feeding of ten needy persons} from {the average of what you feed your families, or clothe them}; that is, clothing ten needy persons, and the clothing that suffices in prayer is what is meant, {or the freeing of a slave} [that is, the emancipation of a slave] who is a believer, as it is restricted in another place. Whoever does one of these three things has thereby released himself from his oath. {But whoever does not find} any of these three, {then let him fast three days}, {that is the expiation of your oaths when you swear}: it expiates them, erases them, and prevents sin. {And guard your oaths}: against swearing falsely by Allah and against excessive swearing; and guard them when you swear from breaking them, except when breaking them is better, for then the completion of guarding is to do the good, and not to let one's oath stand as an obstacle to that good. {Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses}: which distinguish the lawful from the unlawful and clarify the rulings. {That perhaps you may be grateful}: to Allah, since He has taught you what you did not know; so it is incumbent upon the servant to thank Allah for His favor in giving him knowledge of the legal rulings and their explanation.

{90–91} Exalted is He condemns these foul things, and informs that they are from the work of Satan and that they are an abomination (rijs). ﴿So avoid it﴾, i.e., leave it, ﴿that you may be successful﴾; for success is not complete except by abandoning what Allah has forbidden, especially these mentioned abominations: wine (khamr), which is everything that veils the intellect, i.e., covers it with its intoxication; gambling (maysir), which is all contests of chance in which there is a consideration from both sides, such as betting and the like; idols (ansab), which are idols, rivals (andad), and the like, that are set up and worshipped besides Allah; and arrows of divination (azlam) by which they seek to determine their fortune. These four Allah has forbidden and warned against, and He has informed of their corruptions, which call to abandoning and avoiding them:

Among them: they are an abomination (rijs), i.e., impure and corrupt in meaning, even if they are not physically impure, and corrupt matters are those one should avoid and not soil oneself with their filth.

Among them: they are from the work of Satan, who is the greatest enemy of man. It is well known that the enemy is to be guarded against, and his traps and deeds are to be guarded against, especially the deeds with which he seeks to ensnare his enemy, for in them is his destruction. So prudence is entirely in keeping far from the work of the clear enemy and being wary of it and fearing falling into it.

Among them: success is not possible for the servant except by avoiding them, for success is attaining the desired and beloved and being saved from what is feared, and these matters prevent success and obstruct it.

Among them: these things cause enmity and hatred among people, and Satan is eager to spread them, especially wine and gambling, so that he may place enmity and hatred between the believers. For in wine there is the reversal of the intellect and the loss of reason, which calls to hatred between a man and his brothers in faith, especially when accompanied by [abuse] that is among the consequences of the wine-drinker; for it may lead to killing. And in gambling there is one party's domination over the other and taking his great wealth without any exchange, which is among the greatest causes of enmity and hatred.

Among them: these things divert the heart, and the body follows it, from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer, for which the servant was created and in which lies his happiness. Wine and gambling divert him from that most greatly; his heart becomes occupied and his mind becomes heedless in engaging with them, until a long period passes over him while he does not know where he is. What sin is greater and more abominable than a sin that defiles its doer, makes him one of the people of filth, throws him into Satan's deeds and snares so that he submits to him as a humble beast submits to its herdsman, comes between the servant and his success, places enmity and hatred among the believers, and diverts from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer? Is there anything beyond these corruptions greater than them?!

For this reason Exalted is He presented the prohibition of them to sound minds by way of inquiry, saying: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾; for the intelligent person, when he looks at some of these corruptions, restrains himself from them and holds back his soul, and he does not need much admonition nor eloquent warning.

{90–91} Exalted is He condemns these foul things, and informs that they are from the work of Satan and that they are an abomination (rijs). ﴿So avoid it﴾, i.e., leave it, ﴿that you may be successful﴾; for success is not complete except by abandoning what Allah has forbidden, especially these mentioned abominations: wine (khamr), which is everything that veils the intellect, i.e., covers it with its intoxication; gambling (maysir), which is all contests of chance in which there is a consideration from both sides, such as betting and the like; idols (ansab), which are idols, rivals (andad), and the like, that are set up and worshipped besides Allah; and arrows of divination (azlam) by which they seek to determine their fortune. These four Allah has forbidden and warned against, and He has informed of their corruptions, which call to abandoning and avoiding them:

Among them: they are an abomination (rijs), i.e., impure and corrupt in meaning, even if they are not physically impure, and corrupt matters are those one should avoid and not soil oneself with their filth.

Among them: they are from the work of Satan, who is the greatest enemy of man. It is well known that the enemy is to be guarded against, and his traps and deeds are to be guarded against, especially the deeds with which he seeks to ensnare his enemy, for in them is his destruction. So prudence is entirely in keeping far from the work of the clear enemy and being wary of it and fearing falling into it.

Among them: success is not possible for the servant except by avoiding them, for success is attaining the desired and beloved and being saved from what is feared, and these matters prevent success and obstruct it.

Among them: these things cause enmity and hatred among people, and Satan is eager to spread them, especially wine and gambling, so that he may place enmity and hatred between the believers. For in wine there is the reversal of the intellect and the loss of reason, which calls to hatred between a man and his brothers in faith, especially when accompanied by [abuse] that is among the consequences of the wine-drinker; for it may lead to killing. And in gambling there is one party's domination over the other and taking his great wealth without any exchange, which is among the greatest causes of enmity and hatred.

Among them: these things divert the heart, and the body follows it, from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer, for which the servant was created and in which lies his happiness. {92} The obedience to Allah and the obedience to His Messenger are one; whoever obeys Allah has obeyed the Messenger, and whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah. This includes carrying out what Allah and His Messenger have commanded, in deeds and in words, outward and inward, obligatory and recommended, concerning the rights of Allah and the rights of His creatures, and refraining likewise from what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden. This command is the most comprehensive of commands, for as you see, it encompasses every command and prohibition, outward and inward. His saying: {And beware} means: beware of disobeying Allah and disobeying His Messenger, for in that lies evil and manifest loss. {But if you turn away}: from what you have been commanded and forbidden, {then know that the duty of Our Messenger is only to convey clearly}: and he has conveyed it. So if you are guided, it is for your own benefit, and if you do evil, it is upon yourselves. Allah is the One who will call you to account, and the Messenger has discharged what was incumbent upon him and what he was entrusted with.

{93} When the prohibition of wine was revealed, along with its emphatic forbiddance and strict warning, some of the believers wished to know the state of their brothers who had died in Islam before wine was prohibited, while they had been drinking it. So Allah revealed this verse, and the Exalted informed that ﴿there is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾; i.e., no sin or guilt ﴿for what they have consumed﴾: of wine and gambling (al-maysir) before their prohibition. And since the negation of blame includes what has been mentioned and other things, it was restricted by His saying: ﴿when they fear Allah, believe, and do righteous deeds﴾; i.e., on the condition that they abstain from sins, believe in Allah with sound faith that necessitates for them the performance of righteous deeds, and then persist in that. Otherwise, a servant may be characterized by this at one time and not another, so it is not sufficient until he is as such, until his term comes and he remains upon his excellence; for indeed Allah loves the doers of good, the good in worshipping the Creator and the good in benefiting the servants. And this noble verse includes whoever consumed what is forbidden, or did other than it, after the prohibition, then acknowledged his sin, repented to Allah, feared Him, believed, and did righteous deeds; indeed Allah forgives him, and the sin in that is lifted from him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 5, verses 94–96:

{94} This is among the favours of God upon His servants: that He informs them of what He will do, by His decree and destiny, so that they may obey Him, proceed with insight, and that whoever perishes may perish with clear evidence, and whoever lives may live with clear evidence. So the Exalted said: {O you who have believed}: God will certainly test your faith. {God will surely test you with something of the game}; that is, something not much, so that it becomes a slight trial, as a lightening and kindness from Him, the Exalted. And that game with which God tests you is that {which your hands and your spears can reach}; that is, you are able to hunt it, so that the testing may be completed thereby. It is not game that is beyond reach by hand or spear, for then the testing would serve no purpose. Then He mentioned the wisdom behind this testing, saying: {that God may make evident}: a manifest knowledge for the creation upon which reward and punishment are based, {who fears Him unseen}: so that he restrains himself from what God has forbidden, although he has the power and ability to do it, and He will reward him with a great reward, as opposed to one who does not fear Him unseen, who does not refrain from disobedience when it presents itself to him, and hunts what he is able to. {Whoever transgresses}: among you, after this clarification which has severed the proofs and made the path clear, {for him is a painful punishment}; that is, painful and agonizing, which none but God can describe, because there is no excuse for that transgressor. What matters is the one who fears Him unseen, when people are not present with him. As for displaying the fear of God in front of people, this may be out of fear of people, and so one is not rewarded for it.

{95} Then He explicitly prohibited killing game while in the state of ihram, saying: {O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in ihram}; that is, while you are muhrimun (those in the state of ihram) for Hajj and 'Umrah. The prohibition on killing it includes the prohibition on the preliminaries of killing, on participating in killing, on indicating it, and on assisting in killing it. Indeed, as part of this, the muhrim is forbidden from eating what has been killed or hunted on his behalf. All of this is a glorification of this great rite of worship: it is forbidden for the muhrim to kill or hunt what was lawful for him before entering ihram. As for His saying {and whoever of you kills it intentionally}; that is, kills game deliberately, {then} for him {is a penalty equivalent to what he killed of livestock}; that is, camels, cattle, or sheep. One looks for what resembles it among these, and it becomes obligatory upon him to give its equivalent, slaughtering it and giving it in charity. The basis is equivalence, {judged by two just men among you}; that is, two trustworthy men who know the ruling and the aspect of resemblance, as the Companions, may God be pleased with them, did when they ruled that for a pigeon there is a sheep, for an ostrich a camel, and for wild cattle of its various kinds a cow. Likewise, for everything that resembles something of the livestock, there is its equivalent. If it resembles nothing, then its value is due, as is the established principle regarding damaged property. This offering must necessarily be {an offering reaching the Ka'bah}; that is, it is slaughtered within the Haram. {Or an expiation of feeding the needy}; that is, the expiation for that penalty is feeding the needy; that is, the equivalent of the livestock is made into food to feed the needy. Many scholars said: the penalty is valued, and food is bought with its value, and each needy person is fed a mudd of wheat or half a sa' of other grain. {Or its equivalent in fasting}; that is, he fasts a day in place of feeding each needy person, {that he may taste the consequence of his deed} through the obligation of the aforementioned penalty upon him. Whoever returns to it after this, God will take retribution from him. And God is Mighty, Owner of retribution.

It was stated explicitly that God specifies the one who intentionally kills game, although the penalty is incumbent upon both the intentional and the mistaken, as is the legal principle: whoever destroys souls or sanctified property must compensate for it in any case when the destruction was without right, because God has attached to it the penalty, the punishment, and retribution. This applies to the intentional one. As for the mistaken one, there is no punishment upon him, only the penalty. (This is the view of the majority of scholars, and the correct position is what the verse explicitly states: there is no penalty upon one who is not intentional, just as there is no sin upon him.)

{96} Since game includes land game and sea game, the Exalted excepted sea game, saying: {The game of the sea and its food is made lawful for you}; that is, it is made lawful for you in your state of ihram: {the game of the sea}, which is its living animals, {and its food}, which is its dead ones. This indicates the permissibility of sea carrion. {As provision for you and for the travelers}; that is, the benefit in its permissibility for you is that it is for your enjoyment and the enjoyment of your companions who travel with you. {But the game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in ihram}. From the wording "game" it is taken that it must be wild, since a domesticated animal is not game, and edible, since what is not edible is not hunted and is not called game. {And fear God, to whom you will be gathered}; that is, fear Him by doing what He commanded and abandoning what He forbade, and seek aid in His piety through your knowledge that you will be gathered to Him, and He will recompense you: whether you have been mindful of Him, so He rewards you with a great reward, or you have not been mindful [of it], so He punishes you.

{97} He, the Exalted, informs that He made {the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a means of standing (qiyaman) for the people}: by upholding its veneration, their religion and their worldly affairs are established. Through it their Islam is completed, their burdens are lifted, and by intending it they obtain abundant gifts and great kindness. Because of it wealth is spent and dangers are faced, and from every deep mountain pass all kinds of Muslims gather there, so that they get to know one another, help one another, consult together on public interests, and bonds are formed between them in their religious and worldly affairs. God, the Exalted, says: {that they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of God over the provision He has given them of the beast of cattle}. Because the House is a means of standing for the people, some scholars have said: the pilgrimage to the House of God is a communal obligation (fard kifayah) every year; if people abandoned its pilgrimage, every capable person would be sinful, and indeed, if people abandoned its pilgrimage, that which sustains their affairs would cease and the Resurrection would come. As for His words {and the offering and the garlands}: that is, likewise He made the offering (hady) and the garlands, which are the most noble kinds of offering, a means of standing for the people, by which they benefit and for which they are rewarded. {That is so that you may know that God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and that God is Knower of all things}: from His knowledge is that He made for you this Sacred House, because of what He knows of your religious and worldly interests.

{98} {Know that God is severe in punishment, and that God is Forgiving and Merciful}: that is, let these two kinds of knowledge be present in your hearts with certainty and conviction; know that He is severe in punishment, both in this world and the next, toward whoever disobeys Him, and that He is Forgiving and Merciful toward whoever repents to Him and obeys Him. This knowledge produces in you fear of His punishment and hope for His forgiveness and reward, and you act in accordance with what fear and hope require.

{100} That is: Say, [O Messenger], to the people, warning them against evil and encouraging them toward good: ﴿Not equal are the evil and the good﴾ — in every respect. Thus faith and disbelief are not equal, nor obedience and disobedience, nor the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, nor evil deeds and good deeds, nor unlawful wealth and lawful wealth. ﴿Even if the abundance of the evil should impress you﴾ — for it benefits its possessor nothing, but rather harms him in his religion and his worldly life. ﴿So fear Allah, O people of understanding, that you may succeed.﴾ Here He addresses the people of understanding — that is, those with complete intellects and perfect judgment — for Allah the Exalted directs His address to them, and they are the ones who are esteemed and in whom goodness is hoped for. Then He informs that success depends upon taqwa (God-consciousness, i.e., conforming to Allah in His commands and prohibitions). Whoever fears Him attains complete success, while whoever abandons His taqwa incurs loss and misses out on gains.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 5, verses 101–102:

{101} He forbids His believing servants from asking about things which, if they were made clear to them, would distress and grieve them. This includes some Muslims asking the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about their fathers, or about their own state in Paradise or Hell. For such a question, if it were answered for the questioner, might bring him no good. It also includes asking about matters that have not occurred, and questions which entail strict rulings in the Sharia that might embarrass the Ummah, and asking about what does not concern one. These questions and what resembles them are the ones that are forbidden. As for a question which does not lead to any of these, it is commanded, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know﴾. {103} This is a censure of the polytheists who legislated in the religion what Allah had not permitted, and declared unlawful what Allah had made lawful. By their corrupt opinions they made some of their livestock forbidden according to their own conventions, which opposed what Allah had sent down. So Allah said: ﴿Allah did not institute any bahira (a she-camel whose ear they would slit, then forbid riding her and regard her as sacred), nor any sa'iba (a she-camel, cow or sheep which, once it reached a point they had agreed upon, they let loose, so that it was not ridden, nor was any load carried on it, nor was it eaten; and some of them would vow a portion of their property to be let loose as a sa'iba), nor any wasila, nor any ham (a male camel whose back they protected from riding and carrying once it reached a known state among them)﴾. All of these are things the polytheists made forbidden without any evidence or proof; rather, that is a fabrication against Allah and an outcome of their ignorance and lack of reason. Therefore He said: ﴿But those who disbelieve invent lies against Allah, and most of them do not reason﴾, for there is neither transmitted authority nor intellect behind them.

{104} Despite this, they were pleased with their opinions, which were built on ignorance and wrongdoing. When they were called ﴿to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger﴾, they turned away and did not accept, and they said ﴿Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon﴾ in religion, even though it was not sound nor a religion that saves from the punishment of Allah. Even if their fathers had sufficiency, knowledge and understanding, the matter would have been easier; but their fathers did not reason at all, meaning that there was nothing of reason with them, nor any knowledge or guidance. So woe to those who follow one who has no sound knowledge and no sound reason, and who abandon following what Allah has sent down and following His messengers, which fills the hearts with knowledge, faith, guidance and certainty.

O you who believe, take care of yourselves; the one who strays cannot harm you when you are guided. (Qur'an 5:105)

Commentary: {{O you who have believed, upon you is your own self}}; i.e., strive to reform it, perfect it, and oblige it to follow the Straight Path (al-sirat al-mustaqim). For when you are righteous, the one who has gone astray from the Straight Path and has not been guided to the upright religion cannot harm you; he harms only himself. This does not indicate that enjoining good (al-amr bil-ma'ruf) and forbidding evil (al-nahy 'an al-munkar) do not harm the servant if he abandons and neglects them; for his guidance is not complete except by carrying out what is obligatory upon him of enjoining good and forbidding evil. Yes, if he is unable to change the evil with his hand and his tongue, and he denies it in his heart, then the straying of others does not harm him. And His saying: {{To Allah is your return, all of you}}; i.e., your ultimate end on the Day of Resurrection and your gathering before Allah, {{then He will inform you of what you used to do}}: of good and evil.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 5, verses 106–108:

{106} He, exalted is He, informs us, in a statement that carries the command to call two witnesses to a bequest when the signs and precursors of death come upon a person. He should write his will and have two witnesses of integrity, whose testimony is accepted, attest to it: {or two others from outside your own (folk)}; that is, from outside the people of your religion, from among the Jews, the Christians, or others. This is to be done in cases of necessity and emergency, when no others from among the Muslims are available, {if you are travelling in the land} (i.e., you journey through it), {and the calamity of death befalls you}; that is, then call those two as witnesses. He only commanded their testimony to be called because their word in that situation is accepted. They are to be made to stand under oath, by being detained {after the prayer}, which they hold in reverence, {and they swear by Allah}: that they have spoken truthfully and have neither altered nor changed this, {if you doubt}: concerning their testimony. If you believe them, then there is no need for the oath by that. And they say: {We will not sell it}; that is, our oaths, {for any price}: by lying in them for the sake of some worldly gain, {even if it were a near kinsman}: we will not spare him because of his nearness to us, {nor will we conceal the testimony of Allah}: rather, we will render it as we heard it, {for then indeed we would be among the sinners} (i.e., if we concealed it).

{107} {And if it becomes known that the two have incurred sin}; that is, the two witnesses, {by being shown to have committed a breach}: by there being evidence indicating that they lied and betrayed, {then let two others stand in their place from among those who have the right claim against them, the two nearest of kin}; that is, let two men from among the heirs of the deceased stand, and let them be from the nearest of the heirs to him, {and they swear by Allah: Our testimony is truer than their testimony}; that is, they lied, altered, and betrayed. {And we have not transgressed; for then indeed we would be among the wrongdoers}; that is, if we wronged, transgressed, and testified falsely.

{108} Allah, the Exalted, said, explaining the wisdom of that testimony, its confirmation, and its being returned to the heirs of the deceased when betrayal appears from the witnesses: {That is more suitable} (i.e., closer) {for them to bring the testimony in its proper form}: when those confirmations are made binding upon them, {or they fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths}; that is, that their oaths will not be accepted and will then be turned back upon the heirs of the deceased. {And Allah does not guide the defiant people}: i.e., those whose description is defiance; so they do not desire guidance or the aim toward the straight path.

The summary of this: when death approaches a person during travel or something similar, where reliable witnesses are likely to be scarce, he should appoint two upright Muslim witnesses. If he finds only two disbelieving witnesses, it is permissible to appoint them, but for their disbelief's sake; if the heirs come to doubt them, they make them swear after the prayer that they did not betray, did not lie, did not alter, and did not change. Thus they are cleared of any claim directed at them. If the heirs do not accept them and find evidence indicating the witnesses lied, then if the heirs wish, two of them shall stand, swear by Allah that their testimony is truer than the first two witnesses' testimony, and that the two betrayed and lied, and so they are entitled to what they claim from them.

These noble verses were revealed concerning the well-known story of Tamim al-Dari and 'Adi ibn Bada', when al-'Adawi bequeathed to them. And Allah knows best.

From these noble verses several rulings are derived:
First: bequest is legislated, and it is fitting for one whose death is approaching to make a bequest.
Second: it remains valid even if the person has reached the precursors and signs of death, as long as his mind is still intact.
Third: the testimony for a bequest must involve two upright witnesses.
Fourth: the testimony of disbelievers in this bequest and similar cases is accepted due to necessity. This is the view of Imam Ahmad. Many scholars claimed this ruling is abrogated (mansukh), but this claim has no evidence.
Fifth: it may be inferred from the implication and meaning of the ruling that the testimony of disbelievers, when no others are available, is accepted even outside this matter, as Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah held.
Sixth: it is permissible for a Muslim to travel with a disbeliever when there is no prohibited concern.
Seventh: travel for trade is permissible.
Eighth: if the witnesses are suspected and no evidence indicating their betrayal appears, and the heirs wish to bind them with oath, detaining them after the prayer, they swear in the manner Allah has mentioned.
Ninth: if no accusation or doubt arises, there is no need to detain them or impose the oath upon them.
Tenth: the glorification of the matter of testimony, in that Allah attributes it to Himself, and that it must be taken care of and upheld with justice.
Eleventh: it is permissible to test the witnesses when doubt arises about them, and to separate them to examine their testimony.
Twelfth: if evidence indicating the lying of the two executors in this matter is found, two of the heirs of the deceased stand and swear by Allah that our oaths are more truthful than theirs, and that they betrayed and lied; then what they claim is handed to them, and the evidence together with their oaths stands in place of proof.

{109} God, exalted is He, informs about the Day of Resurrection and the great terrors within it, and that God will gather all the Messengers on it and ask them: "What response did you receive?" That is, what did your peoples answer you? They will say: "We have no knowledge. Indeed, knowledge belongs only to You, our Lord; You are more knowing than us." "Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen." That is, You know the hidden matters and the manifest ones.

{110} "When God said: O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My blessing upon you and upon your mother." That is, remember it with your heart and tongue, and fulfill its obligation in gratitude to your Lord, since He bestowed upon you blessings He bestowed upon no one else. "When I supported you with the Holy Spirit." That is, when I strengthened you with the spirit and the revelation that purified you, made you pure, and gave you the ability to carry out God's command and call to His path. It has been said that the Holy Spirit here refers to Gabriel, peace be upon him, and that God aided him by means of him, by his constant company and his steadying him in difficult situations. "You spoke to people in the cradle and in maturity." The speech meant here is not the customary speech that is mere talk, but the speech from which both speaker and listener benefit, namely calling to God. Jesus, peace be upon him, shared in this as his brethren among the steadfast Messengers did: speaking in maturity with the message, calling to good, and forbidding evil. He was distinguished from them in that he spoke to people in the cradle, saying: "Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet, and He has made me blessed wherever I am, and enjoined upon me prayer and zakat as long as I live..." [the verse].

"And when I taught you the Book and wisdom." The Book includes the earlier scriptures, especially the Torah, for he was among the most knowledgeable of the prophets of the Children of Israel in it after Moses, and it includes the Gospel that God sent down to him. Wisdom is knowing the secrets, benefits and rulings of the Sharia, good calling and teaching, and attention to what is fitting in the manner that is fitting. "And when you shaped from clay the likeness of a bird." That is, a bird fashioned without a soul in it. "Then you breathed into it and it became a bird by My permission." "And you healed the one born blind," who has no sight or eye, "and the leper, by My permission. And when you brought forth the dead by My permission." These are clear signs and striking miracles that physicians and others cannot match; God supported Jesus with them and strengthened his call by them.

"And when I restrained the Children of Israel from you, when you came to them with clear proofs, and those among them who disbelieved said: 'This is nothing but manifest sorcery.'" When the truth came to them, supported by clear proofs that necessitate belief in it, they said this. They intended to kill Jesus and strove toward that, but God restrained their hands from him, protected him from them, and preserved him.

These are favors with which God graced His servant and Messenger Jesus, son of Mary, and He called him to be grateful for them and to fulfill them. He, peace be upon him, fulfilled them in the fullest manner, and he was patient as his brethren among the steadfast Messengers were patient.

{111–120} That is: remember My blessing upon you when I made followers and helpers available to you. I inspired the disciples (al-Hawariyyun), that is, I inspired them and placed in their hearts faith in Me and in My Messenger. Or it means I inspired them through your tongue, that is, I commanded them with the revelation that came to you from Allah. They responded to this, submitted, and said: ﴿We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims﴾.
